verdicts.BUG: a real defect with a concrete failure
verdicts.MINOR: correct but weak, worth a cheap fix
verdicts.INVALID: the claim is false, handled elsewhere, or against documented intent
verdicts.SKIP: style, or a change worth less than it costs

findings: every finding of the 19 review batches, merged with its duplicates within its batch
threads: bot review threads on the fix pull requests that were answered without a change

findings.claim: Email verification checks the link's email hash against the request-start user instance but marks the locked current row verified, so an email changed in between gets verified without proof.
findings.reasoning: Laravel's EmailVerificationRequest::authorize (vendor/.../Foundation/Auth/EmailVerificationRequest.php:22) compares sha1 of $this->user()->getEmailForVerification() — the instance the auth middleware loaded at request start. VerifyEmailAction::execute (VerifyEmailAction.php:21-27) re-reads and locks the row but only checks canSignIn/hasVerifiedEmail, never that the locked email is the one the link was signed for. UpdateUserIdentityAction (UpdateUserIdentityAction.php:24-30) can commit an email change (nulling email_verified_at) inside that window, after which markEmailAsVerified confirms the new, unproven address. A confirmed address is load-bearing: ResolveSocialLoginAction.php:88-104 / docs/dev/social-login.md:108-109 sign a provider-vouched owner straight into an account whose email is confirmed and keep its password, while an unconfirmed one is taken over (password removed, sessions ended).
findings.scenario: Attacker registers with own address A and receives A's verification link (reusable for 60 minutes; verify route throttled 6/min, profile PATCH unthrottled). They fire GET verify(A) and PATCH /profile email=B (victim's address, no RateGuru account) in one packet; when the PATCH commits after authorize() but before the lock, B is stored as verified. When the owner of B later uses 'Log in with Google', they land in the attacker's account, whose password the attacker still holds (account pre-hijacking), instead of the claim path that would have removed the attacker's password.

findings.claim: Changing the password leaves every other session and the remember-me token valid, so a stolen session survives the owner's password change.
findings.reasoning: UpdatePasswordAction.php:35-37 writes only 'password'; it neither rotates remember_token nor starts a new users.session_generation. The app already has the mechanism to end other sessions (EnsureSessionGenerationIsCurrent in the web group, bootstrap/app.php:35; used by ClaimAccountWithVerifiedEmailAction.php:116-117), and Laravel's auth.session middleware is not on the web group (only Filament's panel uses AuthenticateSession). ResetPasswordAction.php:39-42 rotates remember_token but also does not bump session_generation, so even the emailed reset leaves existing sessions alive (SESSION_DRIVER=database, config/session.php:21). There is no 'log out other devices' feature, and no doc records keeping sessions as intended.
findings.scenario: An attacker obtains a victim's session cookie (or a 'remember me' cookie on a shared machine). The victim notices and changes the password on /profile (or resets it by email); the attacker's session keeps working indefinitely, and after a plain change the remember cookie also keeps logging them back in.

findings.claim: Login does not normalize the email, so on PostgreSQL a differently-cased address never matches the stored (lowercase) email.
findings.reasoning: LoginRequest.php:30 accepts the email as typed and AuthenticateUserAction.php:23-26 passes it to Auth::attempt, whose Eloquent provider does WHERE email = ? — case-sensitive on PostgreSQL (the primary engine, docs/architecture/database-support.md) and SQLite. Stored emails are lowercase on the self-service paths (RegisterUserRequest.php:19 and ProfileUpdateRequest.php:31 'lowercase', SocialIdentityNormalizer.php:48), and nothing (no prepareForValidation, no custom provider) lowercases the login input; only the throttle key is lowercased (AuthenticateUserAction.php:79). SendPasswordResetLinkRequest.php:16 and ResetPasswordRequest.php:14 have the same gap. Note admin-created emails are NOT lowercased (UserEditor.php:256, CreateAdminUserCommand.php:24), so mixed-case rows can exist. No test covers mixed-case login.
findings.scenario: A member registered as ada@example.com types Ada@Example.com on /login: they get 'These credentials do not match our records'; trying 'Forgot password' with the same spelling returns 'We can't find a user with that email address', leaving them locked out on PostgreSQL while the same input works on MariaDB.

findings.claim: ProfileController::update does not handle CannotUpdateProfileException, so a refused update returns a 500.
findings.reasoning: The bot only names the tombstone race, but the common path is worse: canUpdateProfile() is Active-only (UserStatus.php:89-91; docs/architecture/user-lifecycle.md 'Public profile/identity/avatar mutation is frozen'), UpdateUserIdentityAction.php:20-21 throws CannotUpdateProfileException (a plain RuntimeException with no render/report mapping; bootstrap/app.php registers none), and ProfileController.php:50 does not catch it. resources/views/profile/edit.blade.php includes the identity form unconditionally, so every Limited/Banned/Shadowbanned user is offered a form whose submit crashes. The Livewire EditProfileForm.php:57-62 catches only ImageIngestException, so the same refusal from UpdateUserProfileAction.php:60-61 is also unhandled. No HTTP test covers a sanctioned user saving the profile.
findings.scenario: A Limited user opens /profile, edits their display name/username and presses Save: the write is correctly refused, but they get a 500 error page (and Sentry gets an unhandled exception) instead of a message that their profile is locked while restricted.

findings.claim: manage-project-settings checks only the role, so a Limited/Banned/Shadowbanned admin still passes it.
findings.reasoning: ProjectSettingsPolicy.php:9-12 returns isAdmin() only, against the lifecycle contract (docs/architecture/user-lifecycle.md: privileged capability requires role AND canAccessPrivilegedPanel; 'no role rescues a non-active status'), which PersonaPolicy/StudioPlanPolicy/CategoryPolicy follow. Inside the panel Filament's Authenticate runs on every Livewire request too (vendor FilamentServiceProvider.php:128 adds it as persistent middleware; User::canAccessPanel requires Active), but the gate is also the sole re-check outside a panel request: GenerateProjectTranslationChunkJob.php:103-109 re-reads the starting admin and asks Gate::forUser(...)->allows('manage-project-settings') precisely to stop work for someone who lost the capability (its docblock: 'whoever started the batch may still manage project settings'). ProjectSettingsPolicyTest only covers admin/moderator/user, not a sanctioned admin.
findings.scenario: An admin starts 'Generate missing' translations for a language (many chunks, each one paid provider call), then is banned by another admin; every remaining queued chunk still passes the authorization check and keeps sending content to the AI provider and storing suggestions under the banned admin's batch.

findings.claim: RatingGroupPolicy, RatingOptionPolicy, TagPolicy::delete (and MediaDiagnosticsPolicy) check isAdmin() only, so a sanctioned admin keeps those abilities, and CategoryPolicy's docblock wrongly says every privileged policy checks lifecycle.
findings.reasoning: True as stated: RatingGroupPolicy.php:10-28, RatingOptionPolicy.php:10-33, TagPolicy.php:31-34 and MediaDiagnosticsPolicy.php:9-12 ignore status, unlike CategoryPolicy.php:47-50 (whose fix commit ceaaa73e called the same omission a defect) and the TagPolicy create/update helper. Practical exposure is small: these abilities are only used from Filament pages and the actions they call (CreateRatingGroupAction.php:23, DeleteTagAction.php:24, MediaDiagnosticsPage.php:182, ...), and Filament's Authenticate is persistent for Livewire requests (vendor FilamentServiceProvider.php:128) and denies non-Active staff via User::canAccessPanel (User.php:406-416) on every request. None of these actions re-reads the actor under lock, so the policy is only a second line of defence. The CategoryPolicy.php:36 docblock claim becomes true once these are fixed.
findings.scenario: Defence in depth only: if any of these actions is ever reached outside the panel's persistent Authenticate (a console command, job, API or a future non-panel Livewire component), a banned or limited admin passes create/update/archive/delete of rating groups/options, tag deletion and media diagnostics.

findings.claim: POST confirm-password (and the password-update check) has no attempt limit, so an authenticated session can guess the account password without limit.
findings.reasoning: routes/auth.php:78 registers POST confirm-password with no throttle, and ConfirmPasswordAction.php:13-16 validates the credentials each time; PUT password (routes/auth.php:80, 'current_password' rule in UpdatePasswordRequest.php:15) and DELETE /profile (routes/web.php:72, DeleteUserRequest.php:39) are unthrottled password oracles too, while reset-password, set-link and verification routes carry throttle:6,1. Exploitation requires an already-hijacked session and online bcrypt guessing, so the gain is learning the plaintext password (reuse elsewhere) — low impact, cheap to close. The 'existing shared account-scoped limit' rabbit mentions does not exist; AuthenticateUserAction keys its limit by email|ip for login only.
findings.scenario: Someone holding a stolen session cookie scripts POST /confirm-password with a password dictionary at server speed; nothing slows them down and a weak password is recovered.

findings.claim: AttachStructuredLogContext runs before session/auth and SetLocale, so the shared log context never has user_id and records the default locale.
findings.reasoning: bootstrap/app.php:22-25 prepends AttachStructuredLogContext to the web group, i.e. before EncryptCookies/StartSession, and SetLocale is appended (bootstrap/app.php:34). LogContext::base() (LogContext.php:14, 22-29) is evaluated at that moment, so auth()->id() is null (session not started, recaller cookie still encrypted) and app()->getLocale() is the default; Log::withContext stores that snapshot. This contradicts docs/observability/observability-foundation.md:27-37 ('user_id (if authenticated)', locale). Impact is limited because DomainLogger re-evaluates base() per call (DomainLogger.php build), so only plain Log:: calls (e.g. CreatePostAction.php:164,187) and framework logs carry the wrong context; LogContextTest exercises the class with actingAs, not the middleware order.
findings.scenario: A signed-in Bulgarian-locale user triggers Log::error('Failed to dispatch follower notification job.') in CreatePostAction: the log line has request_id but no user_id and locale=en, so the incident cannot be tied to the user.

findings.claim: The request-id regex rejects dots although the observability doc allows them, and '$' accepts a trailing newline.
findings.reasoning: AttachRequestId.php:54 uses /^[A-Za-z0-9\-]+$/ while docs/observability/observability-foundation.md:17 documents 'alphanumeric/dash/dot, max 128 chars' as preserved, so an upstream dotted correlation id is silently replaced by a fresh UUID. The '$' vs '\z' point is technically right but practically unreachable: HTTP servers (nginx/PHP-FPM) do not deliver header values containing LF. RequestIdMiddlewareTest only covers missing and over-long ids.
findings.scenario: A proxy or client sends X-Request-Id: web.1234-abcd; RateGuru replaces it with a new UUID, breaking cross-system log correlation the doc promises.

findings.claim: Without 'bail', the email closure still runs when email is an array and (string)$value raises a warning that becomes a 500.
findings.reasoning: DeleteUserRequest.php:25-33 lists 'required','string','max:255', closure. Laravel's Validator::shouldStopValidating (vendor Validator.php:1009-1027) only stops after a failed rule for 'bail' or implicit rules, so after 'string' fails the closure runs and (string) on an array emits 'Array to string conversion', which Laravel's error handler turns into an ErrorException (500). Only reachable by a hand-crafted request (email[]=x) from a signed-in password-less account.
findings.scenario: A social-only user (or a fuzzer with their session) sends DELETE /profile with email[]=x: instead of a validation error the request 500s and is reported to Sentry.

findings.claim: The unique username/email checks run before the write, so a concurrent request taking the same value ends in a unique-constraint QueryException (500).
findings.reasoning: ProfileUpdateRequest.php:26 and :34 use Rule::unique before the transaction, and UpdateUserIdentityAction.php:24-30 saves without catching UniqueConstraintViolationException. The DB unique indexes keep data correct; the only effect is a 500 instead of a field error, and it needs two users claiming the same new username/email within milliseconds. Registration already handles this case (CreatesUserWithUniqueUsername).
findings.scenario: Two members rename themselves to the same free username at the same moment; one gets a 500 page instead of 'username already taken'.

findings.claim: The contact form's 'lowercase' rule rejects valid mixed-case email addresses.
findings.reasoning: SubmitContactMessageRequest.php:16 applies 'lowercase' to the visitor's reply address, which is never looked up or stored as an identity — it is only used as reply-to/sender (SendContactMessageAction.php:91-95). The rule therefore only rejects legitimate input; ContactFormTest only uses lowercase addresses.
findings.scenario: A visitor types John.Smith@Example.com on /contact and gets 'The email field must be lowercase.' and may give up instead of retyping.

findings.claim: The request_id container binding/Context should be cleared at the request boundary so later routes such as /up cannot inherit it.
findings.reasoning: The app runs under PHP-FPM (infrastructure/config/php-fpm/*.conf); there is no Octane/Swoole/RoadRunner in composer.json, so every request builds a fresh container and Context, and /up is a separate request. Queue workers never run this middleware and Laravel rehydrates/flushes Context per job. There is no long-lived process in which the binding could leak.
findings.resolution_ru: Бот просит сбрасывать привязку request_id и Context на границе запроса, чтобы /up её не унаследовал. Итог: бот ошибся, приложение работает под PHP-FPM без Octane, каждый запрос получает свежий контейнер, а воркеры очереди этот middleware не запускают.

findings.claim: UpdatePasswordAction's failure is thrown in the default error bag, so the profile form (updatePassword bag) shows nothing.
findings.reasoning: The ValidationException at UpdatePasswordAction.php:27-32 is only thrown when the locked row is gone or cannot sign in (Deleted tombstone or Persona). Such a session never reaches the controller (EnsureAccountIsNotTombstoned.php:27-36 logs it out first), so the only path is anonymization committing mid-request — and the very next request (the redirect back) is terminated by the same middleware, so no bag would ever be rendered. Ordinary failures (wrong current password, a password-less account) are raised by UpdatePasswordRequest with errorBag 'updatePassword' and are covered by PasswordUpdateTest and SocialOnlyAccountPasswordTest.
findings.resolution_ru: Ошибка UpdatePasswordAction уходит в default bag, и форма профиля её не покажет. Итог: бот ошибся, это исключение возможно только при анонимизации посреди запроса, и следующий запрос завершает EnsureAccountIsNotTombstoned; обычные ошибки идут в bag updatePassword и покрыты тестами.

findings.claim: Confirming deletion of a password-less account by typing its displayed email is weak; require fresh re-authentication instead.
findings.reasoning: This is a documented product decision: docs/dev/social-login.md:136-137 ('Deleting such an account is confirmed with its email address instead of a password'), the DeleteUserRequest.php:10-14 docblock, and commit c640b049 which introduced it so social-only accounts can delete themselves at all. The field is a deliberate-intent confirmation, not an authentication factor; a session holder can already change the email without a password (ProfileUpdateRequest has no current_password), so a stronger factor here would not change the threat model on its own.
findings.resolution_ru: Подтверждать удаление аккаунта без пароля вводом email слабо, нужна повторная аутентификация. Итог: бот ошибся, это задокументированное продуктовое решение для social-only аккаунтов; поле подтверждает намерение, а не личность, и более сильный фактор модель угроз не меняет.

findings.claim: The 'string' rule on the auth-surface markers makes non-string values a validation error, contradicting the lenient docblock.
findings.reasoning: Rejecting non-string markers on the form endpoints is pinned as intended behaviour by tests/Feature/Auth/AuthModalLoginTest.php:121-134 ('treats a return path that is not even a string as a failed submission, safely': array _auth_return_to -> redirect '/', guest). Only the OAuth start (SocialRedirectRequest) is deliberately untyped, with its own rationale. Such values only come from hand-crafted requests and the failure is safe (AuthSurfaceContext falls back to the page flow); at most the trait's docblock wording could be tightened.
findings.resolution_ru: Правило string на маркерах auth-surface противоречит мягкому docblock. Итог: бот ошибся, отказ на нестроковые значения закреплён тестом AuthModalLoginTest как задуманное и безопасное поведение; максимум можно уточнить формулировку docblock.

findings.claim: StopStudioPlanAction should re-authorize the administrator inside the same write boundary as the cancellation.
findings.reasoning: The unlocked check is a documented deadlock-avoidance decision: ManagesStudioActions.php:11-22 explains the administrator is asked 'as it is now, without a lock' because the executor locks an action row before any user row, so locking the admin first would invert the order and deadlock. ensureAllowed (ManagesStudioActions.php:26-33) still re-reads the current row and requires manage-studio-plans (lifecycle-aware). Stop only cancels pending work, so a revocation racing it has no harmful consequence.
findings.resolution_ru: StopStudioPlanAction должен перепроверять администратора в той же блокировке, что и отмену. Итог: бот ошибся, проверка без блокировки задокументирована в ManagesStudioActions ради отсутствия deadlock, права всё равно перечитываются, а Stop лишь отменяет ожидающую работу.

findings.claim: (int) on an oversized digit string could resolve to a different post.
findings.reasoning: routes/web.php:27 constrains {post} with whereNumber, and PHP's (int) on an out-of-range numeric string saturates to PHP_INT_MAX on 64-bit, so an oversized id resolves to no post and findOrFail 404s. Leading zeros map to the same post as the canonical id, and PublishedPostDetailsQuery only returns published posts whose share page is public anyway. No other post can be reached.
findings.resolution_ru: (int) на слишком длинной строке цифр может найти другой пост. Итог: бот ошибся, маршрут ограничен whereNumber, переполнение даёт PHP_INT_MAX и 404, ведущие нули ведут на тот же пост, а запрос отдаёт только опубликованные посты.

findings.claim: Strict === ownership comparisons in PostPolicy::update and CommentPolicy::delete fail when PDO returns one id as a string.
findings.reasoning: On PHP 8.1+ (the project runs 8.5) pdo_pgsql, pdo_sqlite and pdo_mysql/mysqlnd all return native ints for integer columns, and Eloquent casts the incrementing key to int, so user_id and id are both ints on every supported engine; the Unit/Feature suites run on all three engines in CI (docs/architecture/database-support.md) including the owner-delete tests. Using (int) casts as the neighbouring methods do would be purely cosmetic.
findings.resolution_ru: Строгое === в PostPolicy и CommentPolicy сломается, если PDO вернёт id строкой. Итог: бот ошибся, на PHP 8.1+ все три драйвера возвращают int, Eloquent приводит ключ к int, а тесты идут на всех движках в CI; приведение (int) было бы косметикой.

findings.claim: The parked social identity should be bound to the original account id and checked against the signed-in user before linking.
findings.reasoning: CompletePendingSocialLinkAction.php:41-43 links only when the signed-in account's normalized email equals the email the identity carried, and users.email is unique, so the pending link is already bound to exactly the account that owns that address; it is one-shot and expires in 10 minutes (PendingSocialLink.php:21, 76-79). This is the documented rule in docs/dev/social-login.md:124-127 ('It only completes when the signed-in account's email is the email the identity carried'). Storing an id would not add a check that the email equality does not already enforce.
findings.resolution_ru: Отложенную social-привязку нужно привязать к id исходного аккаунта. Итог: бот ошибся, привязка идёт только при совпадении email вошедшего аккаунта с email identity, users.email уникален, ссылка одноразовая и живёт 10 минут; хранение id ничего не добавит.

findings.claim: Verify current_password inside the locked password write so a reset committed in between prevents a stale credential from changing the password.
findings.reasoning: Technically a TOCTOU (current_password is validated in UpdatePasswordRequest.php:15 before the lock in UpdatePasswordAction.php:25), but exploiting it requires someone who already knows the old password and holds a session to land a PUT within milliseconds of the owner's reset. The meaningful remediation for that attacker is ending their session on reset/change (01-02); re-hashing under the lock adds cost for no practical gain.
findings.resolution_ru: current_password проверяется до блокировки в UpdatePasswordAction, это TOCTOU. Итог: верно в теории, но нужен человек со старым паролем и сессией, успевший за миллисекунды после сброса; защищает тут завершение сессий (01-02), а не перепроверка под блокировкой.

findings.claim: Connecting a sign-in provider needs no password, letting a session holder attach their own Google identity as a way back in.
findings.reasoning: Accurate, but adding password confirmation here would not close the hole: the same session holder can change the account email without any password (ProfileUpdateRequest.php has no current_password; UpdateUserIdentityAction) and then reset the password, and social-only accounts have no password to confirm. A security email is sent to the account address whenever a provider is connected (docs/dev/social-login.md:192-195) and the card shows and lets the owner disconnect it. The real persistence fix is session invalidation (01-02); this change alone has little value.
findings.resolution_ru: Подключение провайдера входа не требует пароля, и держатель сессии может привязать свой Google. Итог: верно, но пароль дыру не закроет: email меняется без пароля, у social-only аккаунтов пароля нет; владельцу уходит письмо, а реальное решение это инвалидация сессий (01-02).

findings.claim: The password-confirmation flow has no effect because no route uses password.confirm or reads auth.password_confirmed_at.
findings.reasoning: True: grep finds no 'password.confirm' middleware or RequirePassword usage; the routes (routes/auth.php:75-78), view and PasswordConfirmationTest are Breeze scaffolding. Dead code is a cleanup, not a defect; removing it is one way to close the unthrottled oracle in 01-07.
findings.resolution_ru: Подтверждение пароля ни на что не влияет: password.confirm нигде не используется. Итог: верно, это мёртвый код из Breeze; его удаление это уборка, а не исправление дефекта, и один из способов закрыть оракул без throttle из 01-07.

findings.claim: 'string' rules on code/state/error make array-valued callback params fail before the controller, so the user gets a generic redirect and the surface/link context is not cleared.
findings.reasoning: Providers never send array parameters, so only hand-crafted URLs hit this. The leftover SocialLinkContext is still bound to the same account, provider and a 10-minute window and needs valid OAuth state to do anything (SocialLinkContext.php:77-83), and the leftover surface is consumed by the next real callback of that round trip. No security or data consequence; cosmetic only.
findings.resolution_ru: Правила string на code/state/error отбрасывают массивы до контроллера, и контекст привязки не очищается. Итог: верно в теории, но провайдеры массивы не шлют, а оставшийся SocialLinkContext ограничен аккаунтом, провайдером, 10 минутами и OAuth state; последствия косметические.

findings.claim: The connection intent is consumed before OAuth state is validated, so an unsolicited callback (e.g. error=access_denied) can cancel a legitimate connection.
findings.reasoning: Correct mechanically: SocialLinkContext::consume (SocialAuthController.php:71) pulls the context before identityFromCallback, and even a forged code with a wrong state would make Socialite pull the session state (AbstractProvider::hasInvalidState). The consequence is only that the victim's own in-progress 'Connect' fails and must be clicked again; nothing is linked or signed in, and the attacker must time a cross-site navigation into the victim's 10-minute consent window. One-shot consumption 'by the first callback, whatever the outcome' is the documented design (docs/dev/social-login.md:155-157). Value does not justify reworking the callback order.
findings.resolution_ru: Намерение привязки потребляется до проверки OAuth state, и чужой callback может отменить подключение. Итог: верно механически, но жертве лишь придётся снова нажать Connect, ничего не привязывается; одноразовое потребление задокументировано, переделка порядка не окупается.

findings.claim: A failed connection attempt leaves an earlier SocialLinkContext active, so a delayed callback from the abandoned attempt can still attach an identity.
findings.reasoning: Only reachable when gateway->redirect throws (provider switched off, SocialProviderGateway.php:93-97). The surviving context still requires the same signed-in account, the same provider, the 10-minute window and that round trip's valid OAuth state — i.e. the account holder's own consent at the provider for the very connection they started. Completing it attaches nothing the owner did not authorize; no fix needed.
findings.resolution_ru: Неудачное подключение оставляет прежний SocialLinkContext, и запоздавший callback может привязать identity. Итог: верно в теории, но только при выключенном провайдере, и контекст требует того же аккаунта, провайдера, 10 минут и валидного state, то есть согласия владельца.

findings.claim: A signed-in user resetting a different address is redirected to the guest-only login route and loses the status flash.
findings.reasoning: True (RedirectIfAuthenticated bounces /login and the flash ages out), but it needs a person signed in to one account completing a reset for another account; the reset itself succeeds. Purely a missing confirmation message in a rare path.
findings.resolution_ru: Вошедший пользователь, сбросивший пароль для другого адреса, попадает на guest-only login и теряет flash. Итог: верно, но это редкий путь, сам сброс проходит успешно; теряется только сообщение-подтверждение.

findings.claim: 'password-set' is flashed for any same-account reset, so a user who already had a password sees 'Your password is set ... now also sign in with email'.
findings.reasoning: Only reachable when a user who has a password opens a reset link while signed in to that account (forgot-password is guest-only; the set-link button is shown only to password-less accounts, update-password-form.blade.php:1). The message ('You can now also sign in with your email and password') is still essentially true; copy nuance only.
findings.resolution_ru: Сообщение password-set показывается при любом сбросе своего аккаунта, даже если пароль уже был. Итог: верно в теории, но это только если пользователь с паролем открывает ссылку сброса, будучи вошедшим, а текст сообщения по сути всё равно верен; это нюанс формулировки.

findings.claim: Forgot-password reveals whether an email has an account (sent vs 'can't find a user' / throttled), so it should always return one generic notice.
findings.reasoning: Accurate (SendPasswordResetLinkAction.php:14-18, lang/en/passwords.php 'user'), and it is Laravel's default. But registration discloses the same fact on every attempt via 'unique:users' on email (RegisterUserRequest.php:19, unthrottled route), so masking only the reset response gives no real protection; closing enumeration is a product decision spanning registration UX. Personas are already answered generically (PasswordResetTest 'answers as for anyone').
findings.resolution_ru: Forgot-password раскрывает, есть ли аккаунт с таким email. Итог: верно, но регистрация раскрывает то же через unique:users без throttle, так что маскировка сброса не защищает; закрытие перечисления это продуктовое решение вместе с регистрацией.

findings.claim: The StudioPlanPolicy docblock overstates that Content Studio actions re-check on the locked administrator row.
findings.reasoning: Docblock wording: the plan-writing actions do lock the admin, while the Action-queue operations deliberately re-read unlocked (ManagesStudioActions.php:11-22). Behaviour is correct and documented where it matters; a comment tweak at most.
findings.resolution_ru: Docblock StudioPlanPolicy преувеличивает, что действия Studio перепроверяют администратора под блокировкой. Итог: это неточность формулировки, поведение корректно и задокументировано в ManagesStudioActions; максимум правка комментария.

findings.claim: The username regex and 32-char limit are hard-coded instead of using PersonaValidationRules constants.
findings.reasoning: The values are identical today (PersonaValidationRules.php:28,31: '/\A[a-z0-9_]+\z/', 32). Deduplication refactor, no defect.
findings.resolution_ru: Regex и лимит 32 символа для username захардкожены вместо констант PersonaValidationRules. Итог: значения сейчас совпадают, это рефакторинг ради дедупликации, а не дефект.

findings.claim: The share redirect reuses the page query and eager-loads relations it does not need.
findings.reasoning: A few extra bounded eager-load queries on a click-through redirect; reusing PublishedPostDetailsQuery guarantees the share sees exactly what the post page would (the controller docblock's privacy point). The bot itself calls it defensible. Speculative optimization.
findings.resolution_ru: Редирект шаринга переиспользует запрос страницы поста и грузит лишние связи. Итог: это несколько лишних ограниченных запросов, зато PublishedPostDetailsQuery гарантирует, что шаринг видит ровно то же, что страница поста; бот сам называет это оправданным.

findings.claim: PostPolicy::vote/report return true for non-published posts while the actions refuse them via canReceiveVotes/canReceiveReports.
findings.reasoning: The post-state rule is enforced authoritatively in the actions (VotePostAction.php:48-50, re-checked on the locked post) with a clear CannotVoteException message that PostVoting surfaces; the policy expresses actor capability and ownership as docs/architecture/user-lifecycle.md lists it. PostShow only loads published posts (PublishedPostDetailsQuery), so no UI offers voting on a non-public post except one that changes state while open, which the action handles. Consistency refactor without observable effect.
findings.resolution_ru: PostPolicy::vote/report разрешают неопубликованные посты, хотя действия их отклоняют. Итог: состояние поста авторитетно проверяется в действиях под блокировкой с понятной ошибкой, а политика описывает права актора; это рефакторинг согласованности без видимого эффекта.

findings.claim: Catch queue-dispatch failures in the contact controller, restore input and warn that some admin emails may already be queued.
findings.reasoning: A failure to push to the queue (Redis outage in production) surfaces as a reported 500, like every other queued dispatch in the app; the visitor is never told the message was sent, which is the property the controller guards (SubmitContactMessageController.php:21-28). Handling infrastructure outages per controller is out of proportion to the risk.
findings.resolution_ru: Контроллер контактов должен ловить сбой постановки в очередь и предупреждать о частичной отправке. Итог: сбой очереди даёт 500, как везде в приложении, и посетителю не сообщают об успехе, что контроллер и гарантирует; обработка аварий в каждом контроллере несоразмерна.

findings.claim: Category create/update should lock and re-authorize the actor inside the write transaction so a stale administrator cannot write after deletion commits.
findings.reasoning: Create/Update pre-check the policy on the caller (CreateCategoryAction.php:16, UpdateCategoryAction.php:16) and every panel request re-runs Filament's persistent Authenticate (canAccessPanel), so the window is a single in-flight request of an admin who self-deletes or is sanctioned at that instant; the write is non-destructive taxonomy data. Lifecycle docs require locked re-authorization for participation and moderation writes, not taxonomy create/update. Cost exceeds value.
findings.resolution_ru: Создание и изменение категорий должно перепроверять актора под блокировкой в транзакции. Итог: политика проверяется заранее, Filament перепроверяет доступ на каждом запросе, окно в один запрос, запись неразрушающая, а документация требует этого только для участия и модерации.

findings.claim: Password rules should enforce bcrypt's 72-byte limit (and push truncated accounts through a reset).
findings.reasoning: BCRYPT_LIMIT is unset everywhere (no config/hashing.php override, not in .env.example or the infrastructure env templates), so the framework never throws and there is no 500; PHP 8.5 bcrypt silently uses the first 72 bytes. A password whose first 72 bytes are secret is not meaningfully weakened, so a byte-length rule and forced resets have negligible security value.
findings.resolution_ru: Правила пароля должны учитывать лимит bcrypt в 72 байта. Итог: BCRYPT_LIMIT нигде не включён, поэтому 500 не будет, а PHP молча берёт первые 72 байта; такой пароль практически не ослаблен, и правило по длине с принудительными сбросами почти ничего не дают.

findings.claim: The PR description lacks Verification, Architecture Review, Visual Review and Mobile QA sections.
findings.reasoning: A PR-description template check on the audit PR, not a property of the code.
findings.resolution_ru: В описании PR нет разделов Verification, Architecture Review, Visual Review и Mobile QA. Итог: это проверка шаблона описания аудитного PR, а не свойство кода.

findings.claim: Docstring coverage is below the configured threshold.
findings.reasoning: Documentation-coverage metric; no behavioural defect.
findings.resolution_ru: Покрытие docstring ниже настроенного порога. Итог: это метрика документации, поведенческого дефекта нет.

findings.claim: The login lockout check and the failure hit are separate steps around bcrypt, so parallel requests all pass tooManyAttempts and the 5-attempt limit does not hold under concurrency.
findings.reasoning: ensureIsNotRateLimited (AuthenticateUserAction.php:59-75) only reads the counter; RateLimiter::hit runs after Auth::attempt's bcrypt check (:23-27), so N requests in flight for the same email|ip all pass the check before any hit lands. POST /login has no route throttle (routes/auth.php:26), so this limiter is the only one. It is the stock Breeze pattern and the key includes the IP, so it is an amplification of an already per-IP limit rather than a bypass of a strong one.
findings.scenario: An attacker fires 50 concurrent login attempts for victim@example.com from one IP every minute: all 50 pass tooManyAttempts while the counter is still < 5, so the guess rate is ~50/min instead of 5/min.

findings.claim: The sign-in gate evaluates canSignIn() on a possibly stale Auth::user() instead of the persisted row, coordinated with anonymization.
findings.reasoning: Auth::user() here is the instance Auth::attempt just loaded from the database (EloquentUserProvider::retrieveByCredentials) a few statements earlier, not a request-start copy. If anonymization commits in that microsecond window the session it created is ended on the very next request by EnsureAccountIsNotTombstoned, which runs on the whole web group (bootstrap/app.php:34, EnsureAccountIsNotTombstoned.php:27-35) and re-reads the user. Anonymization also scrambles the password, so no later attempt can succeed.
findings.resolution_ru: Проверка входа вызывает canSignIn() на возможно устаревшем Auth::user(). Итог: бот ошибся, это экземпляр, только что загруженный Auth::attempt из базы; если анонимизация успеет в это окно, EnsureAccountIsNotTombstoned завершит сессию на следующем запросе.

findings.claim: The admin panel middleware lacks EnsureSessionGenerationIsCurrent, so a claim that starts a new session generation does not end panel sessions of a password-less account under a non-database session store.
findings.reasoning: The claim revokes old sessions via session_generation (ClaimAccountWithVerifiedEmailAction.php:113-120) plus deleting `sessions` rows, which only works for the database driver (.env.example SESSION_DRIVER=file). EnsureSessionGenerationIsCurrent is appended only to the web group (bootstrap/app.php:26-36); the Filament panel stack (AdminPanelProvider.php:156-170) has only Filament's AuthenticateSession, which compares password hashes and therefore ends the session only when a password existed. SessionGeneration's own docblock promises it 'works for every session driver'. Reaching it needs a staff account with an unconfirmed email and no password, so impact is narrow.
findings.scenario: A moderator account created via an unverified-email social sign-up (no password) is claimed by the mailbox owner through Google; on a file/redis session store the previous holder's /admin session keeps working because the panel never checks the generation.

findings.claim: The pending-email comparison should run after the user lock inside the link transaction and abort if the locked email changed.
findings.reasoning: The only party who can change the email between the comparison (CompletePendingSocialLinkAction.php:41) and the link is the account holder who has just signed in. Linking an identity whose email differs from the account's own address is explicitly allowed (LinkSocialAccountAction.php:28-31: proof is the provider sign-in while signed in), and LinkSocialAccountAction still re-locks the user and refuses an address owned by another account (:50-88). No outcome becomes reachable that the user could not produce directly.
findings.resolution_ru: Сравнение email в CompletePendingSocialLinkAction должно идти после блокировки пользователя. Итог: бот ошибся, сменить email в этом окне может только сам владелец, привязка с другим email разрешена, а LinkSocialAccountAction блокирует пользователя и отказывает при чужом адресе.

findings.claim: Password confirmation has no attempt limit, so a session holder can guess the account password without limit.
findings.reasoning: POST confirm-password has no throttle (routes/auth.php:78) and ConfirmPasswordAction (:11-23) validates the password with no RateLimiter, unlike login, reset and the other credential routes (routes/auth.php:42,68,72,83). Same root cause as batch-01 finding 01-07 (fix once there).
findings.scenario: A stolen session cookie lets an attacker POST /confirm-password with a password list at full speed to recover the account password, then use it on PUT /password to lock the owner out.

findings.claim: The 'email owned elsewhere' check is not atomic with the social-account insert, so a concurrent registration/email change can make the provider email belong to another account after linking.
findings.reasoning: True in principle (LinkSocialAccountAction.php:81-99 checks then inserts, with only identity uniqueness enforced by indexes), but the race needs another account to adopt the provider's address within milliseconds of a link, and the outcome is benign: the identity stays with the account whose holder just proved the provider sign-in, and a concurrent unverified registration of that address is exactly the pre-hijack case the claim flow already handles. An email reservation lock is out of proportion.
findings.resolution_ru: Проверка, что email не занят другим аккаунтом, не атомарна со вставкой social-аккаунта. Итог: верно в теории, но гонка требует захвата адреса за миллисекунды, а исход безвреден и покрыт claim-флоу; блокировка email несоразмерна.

findings.claim: A notification delivery failure after the link commits can block social login; the security notice should be retryable.
findings.reasoning: SocialAccountConnectedNotification implements ShouldQueue with afterCommit() (SocialAccountConnectedNotification.php:18-26), and production uses a real queue (infrastructure/templates/environment/production.env.example QUEUE_CONNECTION=redis), so mail delivery failures happen in the worker with the queue's retries. Only an enqueue failure (queue backend down) can surface here, and since the link has already committed a retry of the sign-in works (no second notify because wasRecentlyCreated is false).
findings.resolution_ru: Сбой уведомления после привязки может заблокировать social-вход, письмо должно быть повторяемым. Итог: бот ошибся, SocialAccountConnectedNotification ставится в очередь с afterCommit и ретраями воркера; при падении очереди повторный вход работает, так как привязка уже закоммичена.

findings.claim: A concurrent or double-submitted registration with the same email escapes as a 500 instead of a field error.
findings.reasoning: The email uniqueness rule runs in RegisterUserRequest (:19) before the ~100ms bcrypt Hash::make (RegisterUserAction.php:27), then User::create inserts; CreatesUserWithUniqueUsername only swallows username violations and rethrows everything else (CreatesUserWithUniqueUsername.php:49-55), and RegisteredUserController/AuthSurfaceContext::guard only catch ValidationException. So the losing insert's UniqueConstraintViolationException becomes a 500. The browser shows the last response of a double-click, i.e. the error, although the account was created.
findings.scenario: A visitor double-clicks Register; both requests pass validation, the first creates and signs in the account, the second hits users_email_unique and the browser displays a 500 page.

findings.claim: A reset token validated for the old email can reset the account after a concurrent email change; recheck the locked row's email and consume the token atomically.
findings.reasoning: Password::reset validates the token for the email, then the callback locks the row and writes (ResetPasswordAction.php:23-45) without re-comparing the email. The window is milliseconds and the token holder controls the old mailbox, so they could equally have submitted the reset a moment earlier; concurrent resets with the same token are by the same holder. Consistent with batch-01 SKIP 01-21 for the analogous password-change race.
findings.resolution_ru: Токен сброса, проверенный для старого email, может сработать после параллельной смены email. Итог: верно в теории, но окно в миллисекунды, а держатель токена контролирует старый ящик и мог отправить сброс мгновением раньше; решение согласовано с 01-21.

findings.claim: Eligibility should be rechecked under the anonymization lock before sending a verification email.
findings.reasoning: If anonymization commits between the check (:13) and the send, the mail goes to the address the requester already owned, and the link it carries is refused by VerifyEmailAction, which locks and requires canSignIn (VerifyEmailAction.php:21-25). No state changes and nothing leaks.
findings.resolution_ru: Право на письмо верификации надо перепроверять под блокировкой анонимизации. Итог: верно в теории, но письмо уйдёт на адрес, которым запросивший и так владел, а ссылку из него отклонит VerifyEmailAction; состояние не меняется и ничего не утекает.

findings.claim: Forgot-password reveals whether an email has an account; return one generic response.
findings.reasoning: Accurate (the broker status is surfaced as a field error, :14-18) but registration already reveals the same fact via the unique email rule (RegisterUserRequest.php:19), so a generic response alone does not close enumeration. Same finding as batch-01 01-29 (SKIP).
findings.resolution_ru: Forgot-password раскрывает наличие аккаунта, нужен единый ответ. Итог: верно, но регистрация уже раскрывает то же через правило unique для email, поэтому единый ответ сам по себе перечисление не закрывает; та же находка, что 01-29.

findings.claim: Verification can confirm a newly changed email with a link signed for the previous address during a concurrent profile update.
findings.reasoning: EmailVerificationRequest::authorize compares the link hash with the request-start user instance; VerifyEmailAction (:16-31) re-locks the row but never compares the locked email with the hash before markEmailAsVerified, while UpdateUserIdentityAction can commit an email change (nulling email_verified_at, UpdateUserIdentityAction.php:24-30) in between. A confirmed address lets social login sign the provider-vouched owner straight into that account. Same root cause as batch-01 BUG 01-01; fix once.
findings.scenario: An attacker registers with own address A, then races GET verify(A) with PATCH profile email=B (the victim's address); when the PATCH commits after authorize() but before the lock, B is stored as verified, and the victim's later 'Log in with Google' lands in the attacker's account.

findings.claim: A terminal (anonymized) account should get an outcome distinct from 'already verified', and the controller should not redirect to ?verified=1.
findings.reasoning: VerifyEmailController redirects to dashboard?verified=1 regardless of the boolean (VerifyEmailController.php:22-24), so a request that raced anonymization gets a cosmetic success flag; EnsureAccountIsNotTombstoned then ends the session on the next request. No state is written for the tombstone. Cosmetic.
findings.resolution_ru: Анонимизированный аккаунт должен получать отдельный исход, без ?verified=1. Итог: верно в теории, но гонка с анонимизацией даёт лишь косметический флаг успеха, для tombstone ничего не пишется, а сессию на следующем запросе завершает EnsureAccountIsNotTombstoned.

findings.claim: Category create/update authorize a possibly stale User and write outside a transaction, so a sanction committed in between still passes CategoryPolicy.
findings.reasoning: Both actions call $admin->can() on the instance Filament loaded for this very request (ManageCategories.php:159-162,280) and CategoryPolicy checks role and lifecycle (CategoryPolicy.php:47-50); the stale window is the few milliseconds of one Livewire request, and the next request is refused. Same finding as batch-01 01-35 (SKIP).
findings.resolution_ru: Создание и изменение категорий авторизует возможно устаревшего User вне транзакции. Итог: верно в теории, но экземпляр загружен Filament в этом же запросе, окно в несколько миллисекунд, а следующий запрос будет отклонён; та же находка, что 01-35.

findings.claim: Category is fully mass-assignable, so the unfiltered payload can set translations, timestamps or the primary key.
findings.reasoning: The only caller builds an explicit four-key array (name, slug, sort_order, is_active) from validated Livewire fields (ManageCategories.php:151-156, and ['is_active'] at :280); no request data reaches create()/update() unfiltered.
findings.resolution_ru: Category полностью mass-assignable, и нефильтрованный payload может задать переводы, timestamps или первичный ключ. Итог: бот ошибся, единственный вызывающий передаёт явный массив из четырёх провалидированных полей Livewire, сырые данные запроса туда не попадают.

findings.claim: The validate-then-insert slug check races; the loser throws an unhandled unique-constraint exception instead of the draftSlug.unique message.
findings.reasoning: Correct that only the Livewire Rule::unique (ManageCategories.php:138) guards the slug before Category::create, but the race needs two administrators saving the same new slug within the same few milliseconds (Livewire serializes one admin's requests per component), and the result is an error toast with no bad data. Not worth a change.
findings.resolution_ru: Проверка уникальности slug до вставки подвержена гонке, и проигравший получает необработанное исключение. Итог: верно, но гонка требует двух администраторов, сохраняющих один и тот же slug в те же миллисекунды, а результат это тост с ошибкой без плохих данных; менять не стоит.

findings.claim: Update should lock and re-read the category and report it missing if it was deleted before the update.
findings.reasoning: ManageCategories re-finds the category at the start of the request (ManageCategories.php:115-122) and refuses a missing one; only a delete committing in the next milliseconds yields an UPDATE of 0 rows and a 'saved' toast for a row that is gone, which the next render corrects. Cosmetic.
findings.resolution_ru: Обновление категории должно перечитывать её под блокировкой и сообщать, если она удалена. Итог: ManageCategories перечитывает категорию в начале запроса; лишь удаление в те же миллисекунды даст тост saved для исчезнувшей строки, который исправит следующий рендер, это косметика.

findings.claim: The whole draft is written without a version check, so concurrent editors silently overwrite each other.
findings.reasoning: Last-write-wins on a four-field admin form (UpdateCategoryAction.php:20) is the normal behaviour for this admin surface; optimistic locking is a feature request, not a defect.
findings.resolution_ru: Черновик записывается без проверки версии, и параллельные редакторы молча перезаписывают друг друга. Итог: last-write-wins на форме из четырёх полей это нормальное поведение для этой админки; оптимистичная блокировка это запрос на фичу, а не дефект.

findings.claim: trim() does not remove Unicode-only whitespace or invisible format characters, so an effectively blank comment passes the empty-body check.
findings.reasoning: AddCommentAction trims with plain trim() (:70-74), whose character list is ASCII only; a body of U+00A0 or U+200B passes and is stored, and CommentForm adds no rule of its own (CommentForm.php:17-31). The repository already recognises this exact problem for moderation reasons and has a normalizer for it (app/Support/Moderation/ModerationReason.php:19-48: 'a reason made of one was stored and displayed as blank forever').
findings.scenario: A member pastes a single no-break space (or zero-width space) into the comment box and submits; a blank comment appears in the thread under their name and counts toward comments_count.

findings.claim: A comment body with an embedded NUL passes validation but cannot be stored in a PostgreSQL text column.
findings.reasoning: True on PostgreSQL (the insert fails with an encoding error and CommentForm only catches CannotCommentException), but a NUL cannot be typed into the textarea; only a forged Livewire payload produces it, and the only effect is a 500 for the forger after the comment rate-limit hit (:60-68). No stored data is affected.
findings.resolution_ru: Текст комментария с NUL проходит валидацию, но не сохраняется в PostgreSQL. Итог: верно для PostgreSQL, но NUL нельзя ввести в textarea, только подделать Livewire payload, и итог это 500 для подделывающего после лимита комментариев; данные не затронуты.

findings.claim: The comments_count recount includes soft-deleted comments; filter deleted_at IS NULL.
findings.reasoning: Comment uses SoftDeletes (app/Models/Comment.php:22), so Comment::query() already applies the global scope that excludes trashed rows; the count is visible AND not deleted, as the docblock says (RefreshesPostCommentsCount.php:12-14).
findings.resolution_ru: Пересчёт comments_count учитывает soft-deleted комментарии, нужен фильтр deleted_at IS NULL. Итог: бот ошибся, Comment использует SoftDeletes, поэтому Comment::query() уже исключает удалённые строки глобальным scope, как и сказано в docblock.

findings.claim: Verify the locked post matches the locked comment's post_id so the wrong post is never recounted.
findings.reasoning: comments.post_id is never updated anywhere (only set at insert, AddCommentAction.php:131-133), and the codebase documents it as immutable (DeleteCommentAction.php:28-29, CommentRetentionPurgeService.php:55, ModerationContentPurgeService.php:106); the post lock keyed by the caller's post_id is therefore always the comment's post.
findings.resolution_ru: Нужно проверить, что заблокированный пост совпадает с post_id заблокированного комментария. Итог: бот ошибся, comments.post_id задаётся только при вставке и нигде не обновляется, это задокументировано как неизменяемое поле, поэтому блокируется всегда пост этого комментария.

findings.claim: A repeat delete of an author-deleted comment that was later finalized throws instead of being a no-op, because the finalized check precedes the trashed() short-circuit.
findings.reasoning: The ordering claim is right (DeleteCommentAction.php:54-65), but the only caller resolves the comment with Comment::query()->findOrFail (CommentsSection.php:169-171), which excludes trashed rows, so a repeat delete of a trashed comment 404s before reaching the action; the throw is only reachable if hide, author delete and an admin finalize all land inside one in-flight delete request.
findings.resolution_ru: Повторное удаление удалённого автором и затем финализированного комментария бросает исключение вместо no-op. Итог: порядок проверок верный, но вызывающий ищет комментарий через findOrFail без удалённых строк и отдаёт 404 раньше; исключение возможно лишь при трёх действиях в одном запросе.

findings.claim: Deleting, hiding or restoring a comment updates comments_count but leaves hot_score computed from the old count.
findings.reasoning: AddCommentAction recalculates the score after refreshing the count (AddCommentAction.php:141-142), but DeleteCommentAction (:77), HideCommentAction (:62) and RestoreCommentAction (:67) only refresh comments_count. HotScoreCalculator weights comments at 0.5 each (HotScoreCalculator.php:11,29) and the hot feed orders by the stored hot_score (FeedQuery.php:85); nothing recomputes it until the next vote or comment, and no scheduled recalculation exists (see the decay finding).
findings.scenario: An author posts 100 comments on their own post over 10 minutes (rate limit 10/min) - raw score +50 - then deletes them all: comments_count returns to 0 but hot_score keeps the inflated value, so the post sits at the top of the Hot feed until someone votes on it.

findings.claim: Hiding an already-hidden comment is an indistinguishable no-op, so the UI shows a success toast and Undo.
findings.reasoning: The no-op return (:54-56) is deliberate idempotency ('Double hide - pre-existing idempotency retained: single log', docs/architecture/comment-lifecycle.md). The report queue pre-checks status and says 'changed meanwhile' (ListReports.php:231-235); only a millisecond race yields a misleading toast whose Undo is a restore the moderator may perform anyway.
findings.resolution_ru: Повторное скрытие скрытого комментария неотличимо от успеха, UI показывает тост и Undo. Итог: no-op это задокументированная идемпотентность, очередь жалоб заранее проверяет статус; ложный тост возможен лишь при гонке в миллисекунды, а Undo это восстановление, доступное модератору и так.

findings.claim: Recipients without a preference get default() instead of LocaleManager::fallback(), ignoring APP_FALLBACK_LOCALE.
findings.reasoning: Choosing the project default is documented intent in the code: the fallback is 'nobody's preference' (SendContactMessageAction.php:39-43) and for the mailbox 'the default language is the only honest choice' (:58-61). LocaleManager distinguishes default() (the project's language, English by policy) from fallback() (the technical key fallback, LocaleManager.php:53-69); mail language is the former by design.
findings.resolution_ru: Получатели без предпочтения получают default() вместо LocaleManager::fallback(). Итог: бот ошибся, язык проекта выбран намеренно и это задокументировано в коде; LocaleManager различает default() как язык проекта и fallback() как технический fallback ключей, для писем нужен первый.

findings.claim: Validate the MAIL_CONTACT_TO fallback and raise the no-recipient error when it is malformed instead of queueing.
findings.reasoning: mail.contact_to is deployment configuration set by the operator (:68); a malformed value is a deployment fault that surfaces in the mail worker's failed jobs. Validating config shape inside a request-time action is hardening of operator input with little value.
findings.resolution_ru: Нужно валидировать fallback MAIL_CONTACT_TO и выдавать ошибку при кривом значении. Итог: mail.contact_to это конфигурация деплоя от оператора, кривое значение это ошибка деплоя, видимая в failed jobs; проверять формат конфига в действии запроса почти бесполезно.

findings.claim: DemoFillSeeder should recalculate counters for retained comments after deleting their votes.
findings.reasoning: The request is about database/seeders/DemoFillSeeder.php (demo data), not the action, which counts correctly under a row lock (:17-38). Demo data accuracy is out of scope for this audit.
findings.resolution_ru: DemoFillSeeder должен пересчитывать счётчики оставшихся комментариев после удаления их голосов. Итог: замечание касается демо-сидера, а не действия, которое считает корректно под блокировкой строки; точность демо-данных вне рамок аудита.

findings.claim: Check save()'s result and throw when it returns false so the vote transaction rolls back.
findings.reasoning: Eloquent save() returns false only when a saving/updating listener vetoes; Post has no observer or model-event listener (no booted()/observe for Post in app/), so the branch is unreachable today. Defensive consistency only.
findings.resolution_ru: Нужно проверять результат save() и бросать исключение при false, чтобы откатить транзакцию голоса. Итог: save() возвращает false только при вето слушателя, а у Post нет ни observer, ни слушателей событий модели, так что ветка сейчас недостижима; это лишь защитная согласованность.

findings.claim: Recalculating vote counters should also refresh hot_score.
findings.reasoning: The vote path already recalculates the score right after the counters (VotePostAction.php:106-107). Only the manual repair command (RecalculatePostCountersCommand) leaves the score, and the separate posts:recalculate-hot-scores command exists for that.
findings.resolution_ru: Пересчёт счётчиков голосов должен обновлять и hot_score. Итог: путь голосования уже пересчитывает score сразу после счётчиков; score не трогает только ручная команда ремонта RecalculatePostCountersCommand, а для него есть отдельная команда posts:recalculate-hot-scores.

findings.claim: The follows.followed log fires on repeat follows that create no row; log only when wasRecentlyCreated.
findings.reasoning: Accurate (firstOrCreate's result is discarded, FollowAuthorAction.php:68-74, unlike SavePostAction.php:63-65), but it only affects an info-level log line for an idempotent repeat; no behaviour or stored state depends on it.
findings.resolution_ru: Лог follows.followed пишется и при повторной подписке без новой строки, нужно логировать только при wasRecentlyCreated. Итог: верно, но это касается лишь info-строки лога для идемпотентного повтора, ни поведение, ни сохранённое состояние от неё не зависят.

findings.claim: Follower notifications are still sent after show_follow_buttons is disabled.
findings.reasoning: docs/follows/follow-authors.md:50-52 states 'Notifications are not generated when feature is disabled', but NotifyFollowersAboutNewPostAction::handle (:42-113) never reads the flag and CreatePostAction/ApprovePostAction dispatch the job unconditionally (CreatePostAction.php:158-160, ApprovePostAction.php:98). Existing follow rows survive the switch, and with the flag off members cannot even unfollow (UnfollowAuthorAction.php:20-22 throws). No test pins the current behaviour.
findings.scenario: An admin turns off show_follow_buttons; followers of an author keep receiving 'X published a new post' notifications for every new post, and the follow UI to stop them is gone.

findings.claim: Offset-based chunk() over a filtered follower query can skip followers when rows leave the filter during a large send; use chunkById.
findings.reasoning: The query filters on follows membership and notify_followed_author_posts (:57-65) and pages with chunk(500), i.e. LIMIT/OFFSET ordered by id. If a follower earlier in the id order unfollows or switches the preference off while a long send runs, every later row shifts one position and the first row of the next page is never visited. Only matters for authors with more than 500 followers.
findings.scenario: An author with 2,000 followers publishes; while page 1 is being sent, one follower in page 1 unfollows. Page 2's offset now starts one row later and the follower that was at position 501 never gets the notification.

findings.claim: Recheck the follower's preference and follow relationship inside the per-recipient transaction, synchronized with unfollow and preference writes.
findings.reasoning: The eligibility read is at most one chunk (seconds) old; a follower who unfollows or opts out in that window receiving one last in-app notification is an acceptable edge. Serializing unfollow/preference writes against the sender would add locking to user-facing paths for no material gain.
findings.resolution_ru: Нужно перепроверять предпочтение и подписку получателя внутри транзакции на каждого. Итог: данные устаревают максимум на секунды одного chunk, последнее уведомление отписавшемуся в этом окне допустимо, а блокировки на пользовательских путях ничего не дадут.

findings.claim: The duplicate-notification check races with a concurrent or redelivered job, so a follower can be notified twice for the same post.
findings.reasoning: Dedup is a read of existing notifications per chunk (:28-40,67-79) followed by inserts in separate transactions; two runs of the job for the same post interleave freely. Such overlap is made possible by the job config: NotifyFollowersAboutNewPostJob has timeout 120s (NotifyFollowersAboutNewPostJob.php:19) while every queue connection's retry_after is 90s (config/queue.php:43,71), so a send that runs longer than 90s is handed to a second worker while the first still runs.
findings.scenario: An author with tens of thousands of followers publishes; the job runs past 90s, Redis releases it to another worker, both runs read 'not yet notified' for the remaining chunks, and those followers get two identical notifications.

findings.claim: Recheck per follower that the post is still published and skip delivery otherwise.
findings.reasoning: The job reloads the post and checks Published at the start (NotifyFollowersAboutNewPostJob.php:25-33, action :44-46). A post hidden during the seconds a send runs yields a few notifications linking to a post that now 404s, which is harmless; a per-recipient post lock would serialize the whole send against moderation.
findings.resolution_ru: Нужно перепроверять для каждого подписчика, что пост ещё опубликован. Итог: job проверяет Published в начале; пост, скрытый за секунды рассылки, даст несколько уведомлений со ссылкой на 404, что безвредно, а блокировка поста на каждого получателя сериализует рассылку с модерацией.

findings.claim: Per-recipient send failures are logged and swallowed, so the job succeeds and its retry policy never re-delivers them.
findings.reasoning: The catch (:96-111) reports and continues, and handle() returns normally, so NotifyFollowersAboutNewPostJob's tries=5/backoff (:15-17) never fire for a failed recipient. The per-recipient transaction locks two user rows (LifecycleSafeDatabaseNotifier.php:40-57), so a deadlock or lock timeout against a concurrent user write is a realistic transient failure. The existing dedup check makes a retry safe for recipients already notified.
findings.scenario: A lock timeout on one follower's row (e.g. a concurrent profile write) makes that recipient's send fail; the job finishes successfully and that follower never receives the notification.

findings.claim: The toggle's own flag guard throws before FollowAuthorAction runs, so the security.feature_disabled_action_attempted event is never emitted on the only path the UI uses.
findings.reasoning: FollowAuthorAction logs the security event before throwing (FollowAuthorAction.php:26-33), but ToggleFollowAuthorAction throws first without logging (:21-23), and the FollowButton only calls the toggle (FollowButton.php:42-62). The event is documented as the signal for 'backend action attempted when feature is off' (docs/observability/observability-foundation.md:162), so it can never fire for follows.
findings.scenario: With show_follow_buttons off, a client keeps posting forged toggle requests; nothing appears in the security log although that is the event meant to surface it.

findings.claim: The follow lookup runs outside the mutation transaction, so concurrent toggles can both apply the same transition.
findings.reasoning: True (:25-38), but Livewire queues a component's requests so one button cannot race itself, and both delegated actions are idempotent (firstOrCreate / delete); two tabs clicking within milliseconds end in a consistent state (followed) that the user can toggle again. No invariant breaks.
findings.resolution_ru: Поиск подписки идёт вне транзакции, и параллельные переключения могут применить один и тот же переход. Итог: верно, но Livewire выстраивает запросы компонента в очередь, а оба действия идемпотентны; две вкладки в итоге дают согласованное состояние, инвариант не ломается.

findings.claim: The direct-image branch neither logs url_import.preview.failed nor returns the unsupported-preview result when its fetch fails.
findings.reasoning: DirectImageImportAdapter throws ImportFetchException on failure (DirectImageImportAdapter.php:19-32), which ImportUrlForm already catches and shows as 'fetch failed' (ImportUrlForm.php:56-57), a correct message for a URL that is itself an image. The only difference from the page branch is a missing warning log line and different wording; no user-visible defect.
findings.resolution_ru: Ветка прямой картинки не пишет url_import.preview.failed и не возвращает unsupported-preview при сбое загрузки. Итог: адаптер бросает ImportFetchException, ImportUrlForm показывает корректное fetch failed; отличаются лишь отсутствующая строка лога и формулировка.

findings.claim: download() bypasses the allow_url_imports feature gate, so remote URLs are still fetched after imports are disabled.
findings.reasoning: Only ImportFromUrlAction checks allow_url_imports (:35-37). UploadPostForm::submit downloads the public, client-settable $importedImageUrl via StoreImportedImageAction::download (UploadPostForm.php:49,90-93) with no flag check, and it does so before validation and before CreatePostAction's upload rate limit (CreatePostAction.php:63-68), so the kill switch does not stop server-side fetches.
findings.scenario: An admin disables URL imports (e.g. because the server is being used to pull large remote files); a member sends a Livewire submit with importedImageUrl set to any public URL and an invalid title, and the server still fetches up to 8 MB per call, unthrottled, before validation fails.

findings.claim: The temp file is created with default permissions and chmod'ed afterwards, so another local process could open it in between.
findings.reasoning: The file is empty until after chmod 0600 succeeds (:75-86); a local process would have to open it in that instant and wait, and what it would then read is an image the server just downloaded from a public URL, which the attacker could fetch directly. No confidentiality is at stake.
findings.resolution_ru: Временный файл получает chmod только после создания, и локальный процесс может открыть его в промежутке. Итог: файл пуст до успешного chmod 0600, а прочесть можно лишь картинку с публичного URL, которую атакующий скачает и сам; конфиденциальность не затронута.

findings.claim: A failed fwrite() raises a notice that Laravel turns into ErrorException, which catch (RuntimeException) does not match, so the partial temp file is never deleted.
findings.reasoning: writeAll calls fwrite (:128-145); on a write error (e.g. ENOSPC) PHP emits E_NOTICE 'fwrite(): Write of N bytes failed', which Laravel's HandleExceptions converts to ErrorException (extends Exception, not RuntimeException), so the catch at :88-95 is skipped. UploadPostForm's catch(\Throwable) (UploadPostForm.php:95-99) runs before $importedTempFile is assigned, so nothing deletes the partial file.
findings.scenario: The temp volume fills during an import; each failed submission leaves a partially written rg_import_*.jpg in sys_get_temp_dir(), making the disk-full condition worse.

findings.claim: A reason with an interior NUL reaches the insert unchanged and fails on PostgreSQL with a 500.
findings.reasoning: ModerationReason::normalize strips only leading/trailing control characters (ModerationReason.php:45-48), so an interior NUL would fail the PostgreSQL insert. But reasons are typed by staff in admin textareas, which cannot produce NUL; only a forged admin request triggers it, and the result is a rolled-back action and an error, not bad data.
findings.resolution_ru: Причина с NUL внутри доходит до вставки и даёт 500 на PostgreSQL. Итог: верно, ModerationReason::normalize чистит только края, но причины вводит персонал в textarea админки, где NUL не набрать; это возможно только при подделанном запросе, и итог это откат и ошибка, а не плохие данные.

findings.claim: DemoCommentsSeeder should not reseed finalized comments as Visible.
findings.reasoning: The request targets a demo seeder (database/seeders), not the action, which only sets moderation_removed_at under lock (:59-68). Demo data is out of scope.
findings.resolution_ru: DemoCommentsSeeder не должен заново сидить финализированные комментарии как Visible. Итог: замечание касается демо-сидера, а не действия, которое под блокировкой лишь ставит moderation_removed_at; демо-данные вне рамок аудита.

findings.claim: FinalizePostRemovalAction ignores save()'s return value; a vetoing model callback would still log finalization.
findings.reasoning: save() can only return false when a saving/updating listener vetoes, and Post has no observers, booted() hooks or eloquent.* listeners anywhere in app/, so the scenario is hypothetical. Checking it would be defensive consistency with RecalculatePostScoreAction.php:30, not a fix.
findings.resolution_ru: FinalizePostRemovalAction игнорирует результат save(), и вето колбэка модели всё равно залогирует финализацию. Итог: у Post нет observers, booted() и слушателей eloquent.*, сценарий гипотетический; проверка была бы лишь защитной согласованностью, а не исправлением.

findings.claim: Validate that every PersonaData has a username before planning the import.
findings.reasoning: plan() receives what PersonaFileReader produced, and the reader validates every entry with PersonaValidationRules::importRules(), which makes username required (PersonaValidationRules.php:66-80, PersonaFileReader.php:160-174) and rejects duplicates (:88-96). A username-less entry never reaches plan().
findings.resolution_ru: Нужно проверять, что у каждого PersonaData есть username, до планирования импорта. Итог: бот ошибся, PersonaFileReader валидирует каждую запись через PersonaValidationRules::importRules(), где username обязателен, и отклоняет дубликаты; запись без username до plan() не доходит.

findings.claim: handle() reports plan->unchanged entries without revalidating them, so a Persona renamed since the plan is reported unchanged instead of created.
findings.reasoning: True (:91), but it only affects the report of an admin-run import when a Persona is renamed between preview and confirm; nothing is overwritten, and re-running the import (documented as safe to run again, :21-23) creates the missing one.
findings.resolution_ru: handle() сообщает записи plan->unchanged без перепроверки, и переименованная после плана Persona числится неизменной. Итог: верно, но это касается лишь отчёта админского импорта, ничего не перезаписывается, а безопасный повторный запуск создаст недостающую.

findings.claim: Category activity and author answers are validated before the transaction, so a concurrent deactivation can attach a post to an inactive category or a removed option.
findings.reasoning: Posts in an inactive category are a normal state ('its posts keep it', ManageCategories.php:176; docs/admin/project-presets.md), so a post created in the same millisecond as a deactivation is harmless. A concurrently deleted category or option makes the insert fail its FK; CreatePostAction cleans the stored image and rethrows (:140-149) and UploadPostForm shows the generic error. No inconsistent data results.
findings.resolution_ru: Категория и ответы автора проверяются до транзакции, и пост может попасть в только что деактивированную категорию. Итог: посты в неактивной категории это норма, а удалённая категория или опция ломает вставку по FK, действие чистит картинку и показывает ошибку; несогласованных данных нет.

findings.claim: The outer-rollback test should also assert the uploaded master file is removed.
findings.reasoning: A test-coverage suggestion, not a defect in the action.
findings.resolution_ru: Тест отката должен также проверять удаление загруженного мастер-файла. Итог: это предложение по покрытию тестами, а не дефект действия.

findings.claim: The idempotent re-delete branch treats malformed author-deletion rows (invalid deleted_from_status) as valid and leaves them stuck.
findings.reasoning: The only writer of deleted_from_status is this action, which records it only after requiring an AUTHOR_DELETABLE status (DeletePostAction.php:63-70); no code path creates the malformed row. The no-op branch writes nothing, so it cannot make any row worse; detecting hand-edited rows is not this action's job.
findings.resolution_ru: Ветка повторного удаления считает строки с неверным deleted_from_status валидными и оставляет их зависшими. Итог: бот ошибся, deleted_from_status пишет только это действие и только из статуса AUTHOR_DELETABLE; no-op ничего не пишет, а ловить правленные руками строки не его задача.

findings.claim: TogglePostSaveAction duplicates save/unsave, skips their audit logs and the show_saved_posts flag, and has no production caller.
findings.reasoning: Confirmed dead in production: the UI uses ToggleSavedPostAction (SavePostButton.php:39); TogglePostSaveAction is referenced only from tests (TerminalUserWriteBarrierTest, PostStaleWriteProtectionTest). Its missing flag check and logs are unreachable. Deleting it and migrating the tests is a cleanup, not a fix.
findings.resolution_ru: TogglePostSaveAction дублирует save/unsave, пропускает их логи и флаг show_saved_posts и не вызывается в продакшене. Итог: подтверждено, это мёртвый код, UI использует ToggleSavedPostAction, а этот класс вызывают только тесты; удаление с переносом тестов это уборка, а не исправление.

findings.claim: The saved-state check runs before the locked save/unsave, so concurrent toggles can both act on stale state.
findings.reasoning: True (:19-32), but Livewire queues one component's requests, and SavePostAction/UnsavePostAction are idempotent (firstOrCreate / delete); two tabs racing end saved or unsaved consistently, and the user can toggle again. No invariant breaks.
findings.resolution_ru: Проверка сохранённости идёт до заблокированного save/unsave, и параллельные клики действуют по устаревшему состоянию. Итог: верно, но Livewire выстраивает запросы компонента в очередь, а SavePostAction и UnsavePostAction идемпотентны; инвариант не ломается.

findings.claim: saved_posts.unsaved is logged even when delete() removed zero rows.
findings.reasoning: Accurate (:53-59) but only an info log for an idempotent repeat; nothing reads it for state.
findings.resolution_ru: saved_posts.unsaved логируется, даже когда delete() не удалил ни одной строки. Итог: верно, но это лишь info-лог для идемпотентного повтора, и никто не читает его как состояние.

findings.claim: Every account deletion scans and JSON-decodes the whole notifications table inside its transaction; filter data->author_id / data->actor_id in the database first.
findings.reasoning: The cleanup chunkById()s over every DatabaseNotification and filters in PHP (:126-137) while holding the account's row lock, so cost grows with the whole site's notification history, not the user's. The comment justifies PHP filtering by engine portability (:123-125), but notifications.data is a json column (2026_05_22_000000_create_notifications_table.php:15) and the codebase already filters it with a JSON path on all three CI engines (NotifyFollowersAboutNewPostAction.php:38 where('data->post_id', ...)).
findings.scenario: With a few hundred thousand notifications, a self-service account deletion hydrates every row in 200-row chunks inside one transaction and can run long enough to hit the PHP/request timeout, failing the deletion while holding the user lock.

findings.claim: UpdateUserLocaleAction should lock and re-read the user and refuse a deleted account, so an in-flight locale save cannot restore locale after anonymization.
findings.reasoning: UpdateUserLocaleAction does write through the caller's instance without a lock (UpdateUserLocaleAction.php:20), but Eloquent writes only the dirty 'locale' column, so the worst outcome is a language code on a tombstone that never signs in or receives mail. It carries no personal data.
findings.resolution_ru: UpdateUserLocaleAction должен блокировать пользователя, чтобы сохранение локали не вернуло её после анонимизации. Итог: блокировки действительно нет, но Eloquent пишет только колонку locale, и худший исход это код языка у tombstone без входа и писем; персональных данных в нём нет.

findings.claim: Changing the email leaves reset tokens keyed by the old address; if that address is later registered, the old token can reset the new account.
findings.reasoning: Reset tokens are keyed by email and delivered to that mailbox, so only whoever reads the old address holds the token, and that person can request a fresh link for any account registered with that address at any time anyway. The account that moved away is no longer found by the old email (the broker looks users up by email), so the change itself already invalidates the token for it. No capability is gained.
findings.resolution_ru: После смены email токены сброса остаются на старом адресе и могут сбросить пароль новому аккаунту с этим адресом. Итог: бот ошибся, токен есть только у владельца старого ящика, который и так может запросить новую ссылку, а ушедший аккаунт по старому email уже не находится.

findings.claim: Missing keys are written as null, so an avatar-only or partial call clears bio/display_name/website and nulls rating_activity_visibility.
