findings.reasoning: The single caller, EditProfileForm::save, always passes the full validated set: ProfileValidationRules returns all four fields (ProfileValidationRules.php:17-25) and the form fills rating_activity_visibility when absent (EditProfileForm.php:50-51). No partial caller exists.
findings.resolution_ru: Отсутствующие ключи пишутся как null, и частичный вызов затрёт bio, display_name, website и rating_activity_visibility. Итог: бот ошибся, единственный вызывающий EditProfileForm::save всегда передаёт полный провалидированный набор; частичных вызовов нет.

findings.claim: The previous avatar is soft-deleted without checking whether other users reference it.
findings.reasoning: Avatar assets are never shared: each upload creates a new MediaAsset (UpdateUserProfileAction.php:66-68, SetPersonaAvatarAction.php:112), and no code assigns an existing asset id to another user's avatar_asset_id. Physical purge additionally re-checks references (MediaReferenceChecker.php:35).
findings.resolution_ru: Предыдущий аватар soft-удаляется без проверки, ссылаются ли на него другие пользователи. Итог: бот ошибся, аватары никогда не общие, каждая загрузка создаёт новый MediaAsset, а физическая очистка дополнительно перепроверяет ссылки через MediaReferenceChecker.

findings.claim: A stored avatar file is not cleaned up if an enclosing transaction later rolls back.
findings.reasoning: No caller wraps this action in a transaction: its only caller is EditProfileForm::save (EditProfileForm.php:57), and the code says so (UpdateUserProfileAction.php:102-104). The action's own transaction failure already triggers deleteIfUnclaimed (:85-93).
findings.resolution_ru: Сохранённый файл аватара не убирается, если внешняя транзакция потом откатится. Итог: бот ошибся, никто не оборачивает это действие в транзакцию, единственный вызывающий EditProfileForm::save, а при сбое собственной транзакции действие уже вызывает deleteIfUnclaimed.

findings.claim: The profile log is emitted before an outer transaction commits.
findings.reasoning: There is no outer transaction (sole caller EditProfileForm::save, EditProfileForm.php:57); the log line runs after the action's own transaction has committed (:46-98).
findings.resolution_ru: Лог профиля пишется до коммита внешней транзакции. Итог: бот ошибся, внешней транзакции нет, единственный вызывающий EditProfileForm::save, а строка лога идёт после коммита собственной транзакции действия.

findings.claim: The comment claiming QUEUE_CONNECTION=sync is the only connection is wrong; production uses redis.
findings.reasoning: The comment is indeed outdated (production.env.example sets QUEUE_CONNECTION=redis; the same sentence is in CreatePostAction.php:183-186), but it is a comment; the catch block behaves correctly for both sync and async drivers.
findings.resolution_ru: Комментарий, что QUEUE_CONNECTION=sync единственное соединение, неверен, в продакшене redis. Итог: комментарий действительно устарел (та же фраза есть в CreatePostAction), но это только комментарий, блок catch корректно работает и с sync, и с асинхронными драйверами.

findings.claim: RecalculatePostScoreAction refreshes and saves without locking the post, so the standalone hot-score command can overwrite a concurrent vote's newer score with one computed from stale counters.
findings.reasoning: Inside VotePostAction and AddCommentAction the caller holds the post lock, but posts:recalculate-hot-scores calls handle() with no transaction (RecalculateHotScoresCommand.php:29-34), so refresh() (:17) can read counters just before a vote commits and the later save writes the older score. Only hot_score is written, so counters stay correct and the error lasts until the next activity or run; it becomes routine once the command is scheduled (see the decay finding).
findings.scenario: While the recalculation command runs, a post receives a vote: the command read the pre-vote counters, the vote commits its score, then the command saves the pre-vote score over it.

findings.claim: Inactive posts' hot scores never decay with age, because hot_score is only recalculated on activity.
findings.reasoning: HotScoreCalculator divides by (age+2)^1.5 at calculation time (HotScoreCalculator.php:31-34), but the score is stored (posts.hot_score) and only recomputed on a vote or new comment (VotePostAction.php:107, AddCommentAction.php:142). posts:recalculate-hot-scores exists but is not scheduled (routes/console.php schedules media/posts/comments purges and studio:dispatch-due only). The Hot feed orders by the stored value (FeedQuery.php:85) and is a main navigation entry (lang/en/ui.php nav.hot); docs promise 'Age decreases score' (docs/ranking/phase-33-hot-score-ranking-review.md) and the admin settings describe Hot as 'Recent posts with fast-growing votes first'.
findings.scenario: A post that got 20 upvotes in its first two hours a month ago keeps hot_score 21/4^1.5 = 2.6 forever; a post published today with 5 upvotes after one hour scores 1.15, so the month-old post stays above it in Hot indefinitely, and Hot drifts into a list of posts that peaked early.

findings.claim: The option key uniqueness check runs before the group lock, so concurrent creates with the same key end in an unhandled unique-index exception.
findings.reasoning: Only the Livewire Rule::unique (EditRatingGroup.php saveOption) guards the key before the locked create (:27-33). The race needs two administrators creating the same key in the same group within milliseconds; the outcome is an error, with the unique index keeping data correct.
findings.resolution_ru: Уникальность ключа опции проверяется до блокировки группы, и параллельное создание даёт необработанное исключение индекса. Итог: верно, но нужны два администратора с одним ключом в одной группе за миллисекунды; итог это ошибка, а уникальный индекс сохраняет данные.

findings.claim: The delete guard checks only votes; an option used as a post author answer but with no votes passes, then delete() hits the restrict foreign key and the admin gets an uncaught 500.
findings.reasoning: DeleteRatingOptionAction checks $locked->votes()->exists() (rating_votes only, RatingOption.php:44-47) before $locked->delete() (:32-42). post_author_answers references the option with restrictOnDelete (2026_07_09_100000_create_post_author_answers_table.php:21-24). EditRatingGroup::askToDeleteOption also only checks votes and offers 'delete', and deleteOption catches only CannotDeleteVotedRatingOptionException and InvalidRatingGroupConfigurationException, so the QueryException becomes a 500. No test covers an option with author answers.
findings.scenario: An author picks a new option as their answer on a post that nobody has voted on yet; an admin deletes that option in Rating groups, confirms the dialog, and gets a server error instead of the 'archive it instead' explanation.

findings.claim: Unarchive deactivates any option passed to it, not just archived ones, without the group-minimum check.
findings.reasoning: handle() sets ['archived_at' => null, 'is_active' => false] on whatever option it finds (:26-30) and never runs ValidateRatingOptionTransitionAction, unlike Archive/Delete/Update. EditRatingGroup::unarchiveOption (public Livewire method) does not check archived_at either before calling it.
findings.scenario: An admin has the group page open in two tabs; in tab B they unarchive and then activate option X; back in stale tab A they click Unarchive on X, which silently deactivates the now-active option and leaves the group below its minimum of active options.

findings.claim: UpdateRatingOptionAction can activate an archived option, and VoteRatingOptionAction then accepts votes for it because it checks only is_active.
findings.reasoning: The action validates only the min/max transition (:30-34) and never looks at archived_at, while ActivateRatingOptionRaisingMaximumAction refuses archived options (:38-40). The UI pre-checks archived_at on a freshly loaded row (EditRatingGroup setOptionActive and activeLock), so only a race with a concurrent Archive gets through; but RatingOption::scopeActive and VoteRatingOptionAction (:103-105) treat is_active as the sole availability flag, so an archived-and-active row would be shown and votable.
findings.scenario: Admin A archives option X while admin B's activate click for X is between its fresh read and the group lock; B's update sets is_active=true on the archived row, and members can vote for an option the admin archived.

findings.claim: Mass assignment lets a caller change rating_group_id after validation counted only the original group.
findings.reasoning: Both callers pass explicit arrays - label, description, sort_order, is_active from saveOption, or ['is_active' => ...] from setOptionActive (EditRatingGroup.php saveOption $data and :518) - so rating_group_id never reaches update(). The bot's scenario requires a caller that does not exist.
findings.resolution_ru: Mass assignment позволяет вызывающему сменить rating_group_id после валидации по исходной группе. Итог: бот ошибся, оба вызывающих передают явные массивы полей из saveOption и setOptionActive, rating_group_id в update() не попадает; сценарий требует несуществующего вызывающего.

findings.claim: The vote ability (not own post) should be rechecked after locking, against the locked actor and post.
findings.reasoning: Both halves of PostPolicy::vote are covered after the lock: canVote() is re-evaluated on the locked actor (:69-73), and post ownership is immutable (posts.user_id is never reassigned; ReportContentAction.php:58-59 relies on the same fact), so the pre-lock own-post check cannot go stale.
findings.resolution_ru: Право голосовать (не за свой пост) надо перепроверять после блокировки. Итог: бот ошибся, canVote() перепроверяется на заблокированном акторе, а posts.user_id никогда не переназначается, поэтому проверка своего поста до блокировки не устаревает.

findings.claim: When the guarded UPDATE matches zero rows, Ignore/Resolve return normally, so the caller reports success and offers Undo for a close that did not happen.
findings.reasoning: Both actions compute $updated but return void either way (IgnoreReportAction.php:53-55, ResolveReportAction.php:50-52). ListReports::close pre-checks status Open (ListReports.php:386-390) but a concurrent close in the milliseconds after that read makes the UPDATE match nothing, and close() then toasts 'ignored/resolved' with an Undo that runs ReopenReportAction, which reopens any closed report (ReopenReportAction.php:40-48).
findings.scenario: Moderator A resolves report #12 while moderator B's Ignore for #12 is already past the status pre-check; B sees 'Report #12 ignored' with Undo, clicks Undo, and reopens the report, wiping A's resolution.

findings.claim: Reopening wipes resolved_by/resolved_at/resolution_note with no audit record of the earlier decision.
findings.reasoning: Documented intent: 'Who closed it, when and with which note go with the decision; the report is as it was when it came in' (ReopenReportAction.php:13-17), pinned by ReopenReportActionTest ('without who closed it, when or why'). The migration comment the bot cites (create_reports_table.php:28-29) is about keeping the actor FK on account deletion, not about reopen history.
findings.resolution_ru: Переоткрытие жалобы стирает resolved_by, resolved_at и resolution_note без записи о прежнем решении. Итог: бот ошибся, это задокументированный замысел, закреплённый ReopenReportActionTest; цитируемый комментарий миграции касается FK актора при удалении аккаунта.

findings.claim: Self-reporting is blocked only in the UI for comments and user profiles; the action refuses it only for posts.
findings.reasoning: Posts go through PostPolicy::report, which excludes the owner (ReportContentAction.php:58-62, PostPolicy.php:67-71), but comments and users get no ownership check (:50-52, :64-68, :106-118). ReportModal's reportableType/reportableId are plain public Livewire properties (ReportModal.php:19-21) and resolveReportable accepts any visible comment or any user (:64-84), so a forged request reports one's own content.
findings.scenario: A member forges the report modal payload to report their own comment or their own account; each lands in the moderation queue and bumps the comment's reports_count, adding noise moderators must triage.

findings.claim: Resolve matches status != resolved, so it can overwrite an ignored report and its processor metadata, unlike Ignore which requires status = open.
findings.reasoning: ResolveReportAction updates where status != Resolved (:39-47) while IgnoreReportAction requires Open (IgnoreReportAction.php:42-44) and both claim the same 'first writer wins' convention (IgnoreReportAction.php:26-32). The UI never offers Resolve on an ignored report (ListReports::close pre-checks Open), so only a race reaches it, but then the ignore decision and its moderator are silently replaced. No test pins resolving an ignored report.
findings.scenario: Moderator B ignores report #7 with a note; moderator A, whose Resolve click passed the Open pre-check a moment earlier, overwrites it: the report now says 'Resolved by A' and B's note is gone.

findings.claim: A preset settings key named static_pages would overwrite the project's static pages despite the comment saying they are kept.
findings.reasoning: Only language-policy keys are stripped (:31,51), so a static_pages key would pass through fill() (:81). But presets are operator-authored config applied by the rateguru:setup CLI (SetupProjectPresetCommand), no built-in preset has the key and none ever did (git log -S static_pages on config/project_presets.php is empty), and the documented preset shape has no such key (docs/admin/project-presets.md). Hardening of operator input only.
findings.resolution_ru: Ключ static_pages в пресете перезапишет статические страницы вопреки комментарию. Итог: верно в теории, но пресеты это конфиг оператора для CLI rateguru:setup, ни один встроенный пресет такого ключа не имел, и в документированной структуре его нет; это укрепление ввода оператора.

findings.claim: Preset feature_flags should exclude content_studio_execution_enabled and content_studio_verified_adults so a preset can never enable Studio controls.
findings.reasoning: No built-in preset contains either flag (config/project_presets.php), and only an operator with shell access who edits config and runs rateguru:setup could add one. Applying a preset replaces feature_flags wholesale (:54-58), which can only switch the executor off. Hardening of operator-controlled config.
findings.resolution_ru: feature_flags пресета должны исключать content_studio_execution_enabled и content_studio_verified_adults. Итог: встроенные пресеты их не содержат, добавить их может лишь оператор с shell, а пресет заменяет флаги целиком и может только выключить исполнитель.

findings.claim: Re-applying a preset overwrites archived_at on options already archived, losing their original archive time.
findings.reasoning: True (:148), but it only happens on a deliberate --force reset run from the CLI and only changes a display timestamp on already-archived options; nothing depends on the original value.
findings.resolution_ru: Повторное применение пресета перезаписывает archived_at у уже архивированных опций. Итог: верно, но это происходит только при намеренном сбросе с --force из CLI и меняет лишь отображаемую метку времени; от исходного значения ничего не зависит.

findings.claim: Validate each preset group's active option count (2..15) inside the transaction before committing.
findings.reasoning: Preset contents are developer/operator config, and the shipped presets are checked by tests/Feature/Support/Settings/ProjectPresetsConfigTest.php. Validating config shape inside the apply transaction is a nice-to-have for custom presets.
findings.resolution_ru: Нужно проверять число активных опций в группах пресета (2..15) внутри транзакции. Итог: пресеты это конфиг разработчика или оператора, поставляемые проверяет ProjectPresetsConfigTest; проверка при применении лишь приятное дополнение для своих пресетов.

findings.claim: An explicit empty tags list keeps all existing tags although only null means 'leave tags unchanged'.
findings.reasoning: applyTags returns early for both null and [] (:200-202). The preset documentation says 'Set categories, rating_groups, or tags to null to keep the corresponding records unchanged' and that 'non-configured tags are removed' (docs/admin/project-presets.md), and applyCategories/applyRatingGroups treat only null as a no-op (:110,143).
findings.scenario: An operator writes a custom preset with 'tags' => [] to start without tags and runs rateguru:setup --force; every old tag survives and the command reports 0 tags removed.

findings.claim: Reject presets whose tag names produce duplicate slugs, so neither tag silently overwrites the other.
findings.reasoning: A collision needs two tag names in operator-authored config that slugify identically; the second updateOrCreate wins and the count is off by one. Config validation, not a runtime defect.
findings.resolution_ru: Нужно отклонять пресеты, чьи имена тегов дают одинаковые slug. Итог: коллизия требует двух имён в конфиге оператора с одинаковым slug, тогда побеждает второй updateOrCreate и счётчик расходится на единицу; это валидация конфига, а не дефект выполнения.

findings.claim: SaveProjectSettingsAction does not refuse content_studio_execution_enabled in feature_flags, so the executor can be switched on outside SwitchStudioExecutionAction.
findings.reasoning: Its only caller passes the validated array, and ProjectSettingsPage validates exactly the flags it shows ('Each flag ... and nothing a request adds beside them', ProjectSettingsPage.php:253-256), so an extra flag key is dropped by validate(); the action then merges onto stored flags and keeps the executor switch as stored (SaveProjectSettingsAction.php:56-61).
findings.resolution_ru: SaveProjectSettingsAction не отклоняет content_studio_execution_enabled, и исполнитель можно включить в обход SwitchStudioExecutionAction. Итог: бот ошибся, ProjectSettingsPage валидирует ровно показанные флаги и отбрасывает лишние, а действие сохраняет переключатель как был.

findings.claim: A malformed static-page entry (non-array en, or a page given as []) silently erases that page's stored English.
findings.reasoning: The only caller requires static_pages.{key}.en.title and .content for every page key (ProjectSettingsPage.php:262-269) and passes only validated data, so a malformed or empty English entry cannot reach englishPages().
findings.resolution_ru: Кривая запись статической страницы молча стирает сохранённый английский текст. Итог: бот ошибся, единственный вызывающий требует en.title и en.content для каждой страницы и передаёт только провалидированные данные, кривая запись до englishPages() не дойдёт.

findings.claim: The 'already offered' decision and catalog check run before the row lock, so a concurrent change can let a broken language skip the check.
findings.reasoning: True (:54-60 before lockedRow at :63), but it requires two administrators changing languages concurrently while one language's catalog is broken by a release; the catalog check is a release-safety net, and the Languages page shows catalog problems anyway.
findings.resolution_ru: Решение 'уже предложен' и проверка каталога идут до блокировки строки, и сломанный язык может проскочить. Итог: верно, но нужны два администратора, одновременно меняющие языки при сломанном каталоге; проверка лишь страховка релиза, а страница Languages и так показывает проблемы.

findings.claim: Preflight re-reads Persona state from the transaction snapshot instead of the locked Persona rows.
findings.reasoning: The transaction's first statements are the per-row SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on admin, author and every participant (ApproveStudioPlanAction.php:93-95, LocksUsersInOrder.php:27-33). On PostgreSQL (READ COMMITTED) every later read sees the latest committed rows; on MariaDB the first consistent read (and so the snapshot) happens only after those locks are held, and locked rows cannot change afterwards. The preflight therefore sees the locked state.
findings.resolution_ru: Preflight читает состояние Persona из снимка транзакции, а не из заблокированных строк. Итог: бот ошибся, транзакция начинается с SELECT ... FOR UPDATE по участникам; PostgreSQL READ COMMITTED видит свежие строки, а на MariaDB снимок берётся уже после блокировок.

findings.claim: A logging failure in the after-commit callback can escape and prevent the dispatcher wake.
findings.reasoning: Registration order is approved() log then wake (:142-143), so a throwing logger would skip the wake and surface an error after the approval committed. Log-writer failure is an infrastructure fault, and the documented recovery is the every-minute studio:dispatch-due schedule (routes/console.php), so the post still goes out within a minute.
findings.resolution_ru: Сбой логирования в after-commit колбэке может помешать разбудить диспетчер. Итог: верно, падающий логгер пропустит wake после коммита, но это авария инфраструктуры, а документированное восстановление это ежеминутный studio:dispatch-due, так что пост всё равно уйдёт в течение минуты.

findings.claim: Cancelling a Failed or Held action overwrites failure_code and nulls failure_reason, losing why it stopped.
findings.reasoning: Documented behaviour: Cancel makes the action 'cancelled for good, cancelled_by_administrator' (docs/architecture/studio-plans.md:1843-1846). The earlier stop is recorded in the studio.action.held/.failed log events (docs/architecture/studio-plans.md:1731), and the 'stays as the record' sentence the bot cites (:1400) is about rows never being deleted.
findings.resolution_ru: Отмена Failed или Held действия перезаписывает failure_code и обнуляет failure_reason. Итог: бот ошибся, это задокументированное поведение Cancel, а прежняя остановка записана в событиях studio.action.held/.failed; цитата бота о записи касается неудаляемости строк.

findings.claim: viewAdmin authorizes sanctioned staff because it checks only the role.
findings.reasoning: Accurate, but viewAdmin has no production consumer: it is referenced only by tests (UserPolicyTest, UserPolicyRegistrationTest), and panel access is decided by User::canAccessPanel, which requires both role and an Active-eligible status (User.php:406-417). Unused ability; tightening or deleting it is cleanup.
findings.resolution_ru: viewAdmin пропускает санкционированный персонал, так как проверяет только роль. Итог: верно, но в продакшене viewAdmin никто не использует, только тесты, а доступ к панели решает User::canAccessPanel с проверкой роли и статуса; ужесточение или удаление это уборка.

findings.claim: The PR description lacks Verification, Architecture Review, Visual Review and Mobile QA sections.
findings.reasoning: Audit-PR bookkeeping, not a code finding.
findings.resolution_ru: В описании PR нет разделов Verification, Architecture Review, Visual Review и Mobile QA. Итог: это служебное оформление аудитного PR, а не находка по коду.

findings.claim: The 'tag still used by posts' guard uses posts(), which hides soft-deleted posts, so a tag used only by author-deleted posts is deleted and the post_tag rows cascade away.
findings.reasoning: Post uses SoftDeletes (app/Models/Post.php:31), so $locked->posts()->exists() (DeleteTagAction.php:35) ignores author-deleted posts, and post_tag cascades on tag delete (2026_05_14_183853_create_post_tag_table.php:21). Author-deleted posts are restorable for the retention window and RestoreDeletedPostAction promises 'child data ... was never touched, so it needs no restore' (RestoreDeletedPostAction.php:16-19; docs/architecture/post-lifecycle.md 'Public state during retention'). ManageTags counts posts with the same scope (withCount('posts'), ManageTags.php:267), so such a tag is listed as unused and offered for deletion. This contradicts the action's own contract 'blocked while any post still references the tag. The pivot is never silently detached' (DeleteTagAction.php:15-17); DeleteTagActionTest covers only a live post.
findings.scenario: A member deletes their post tagged #foo (soft delete, restorable for 30 days). An admin sees #foo with 0 posts and deletes it; the post_tag row cascades. The member restores the post from Recently Deleted and it comes back without its tag.

findings.claim: TagPolicy::delete checks only isAdmin(), so a sanctioned (Limited/Banned/Shadowbanned) administrator keeps the ability to delete tags; the check also runs outside the transaction.
findings.reasoning: Same root cause as batch-01 MINOR 01-06, which already named TagPolicy::delete: TagPolicy.php:31-34 returns isAdmin() while create/update use canCurate() with canAccessPrivilegedPanel() (:36-40). Exposure stays small for the reason given there: the only caller is the Filament ManageTags page (ManageTags.php:190), and Filament's persistent Authenticate denies non-Active staff on every Livewire request. The pre-transaction check is the same accepted stale-actor window as 01-35/02-14; only the lifecycle half is worth fixing.
findings.scenario: A Banned administrator whose panel session is somehow still served (or a future non-panel caller) can delete tags, unlike create/update which refuse them.

findings.claim: Tag create/update authorize a possibly stale actor and write outside a transaction, so a sanction racing the request can still create or edit a tag.
findings.reasoning: Same finding as batch-01 01-35 / batch-02 02-14 (SKIP) for categories: the policy (TagPolicy::canCurate, role AND lifecycle, TagPolicy.php:36-40) runs on the instance Filament loaded for this very request, ManageTags re-checks on every request via Filament's persistent Authenticate, and the window is the milliseconds of one in-flight request writing non-destructive taxonomy.
findings.resolution_ru: Создание и изменение тегов авторизует возможно устаревшего актора вне транзакции. Итог: верно в теории, но это та же находка, что 01-35 и 02-14: TagPolicy проверяет роль и статус на экземпляре этого запроса, Filament перепроверяет каждый запрос, окно в миллисекунды.

findings.claim: Concurrent tag saves can both pass UniqueEffectiveTagSlug and the loser hits the tags.slug unique index as an unhandled exception instead of a draftSlug error.
findings.reasoning: True mechanically (ManageTags.php:131 validates, then CreateTagAction.php:24 / UpdateTagAction.php:23 write; tags.slug is unique), but it is the same admin-surface race as batch-02 02-16 (SKIP, category slug): it needs two staff members saving the same new slug within milliseconds, Livewire serializes one user's requests, and the unique index keeps data correct; the only effect is an error toast.
findings.resolution_ru: Параллельные сохранения тега проходят UniqueEffectiveTagSlug, и проигравший ловит исключение уникального индекса. Итог: верно, но это та же гонка, что 02-16: два сотрудника с одним slug за миллисекунды, индекс сохраняет данные, итог лишь тост с ошибкой.

findings.claim: A username/email claimed by another account after UserEditor's unique validation makes $locked->save() throw a unique-constraint exception that surfaces as a 500.
findings.reasoning: UserEditor validates username/email uniqueness (UserEditor.php:119-126) before UpdateUserAccountAction locks and saves (UpdateUserAccountAction.php:45-74); a UniqueConstraintViolationException is not caught there and UserEditor catches only CannotUpdateUserAccountException (UserEditor.php:147-152). Same pattern and verdict as batch-01 MINOR 01-11 on the self-service identity form (same users unique columns, same competing writers: any registration or profile email change). Data stays correct thanks to the indexes.
findings.scenario: An admin changes a user's email to x@example.com while, in the same instant, someone registers or switches their profile to x@example.com; the admin's save ends in a 500 instead of 'Another account uses this email address.'

findings.claim: The locale write is unlocked, so a stale request can write a locale onto an account anonymized in between.
findings.reasoning: Same finding as batch-02 02-56 (SKIP): UpdateUserLocaleAction.php:20 updates the caller's instance without a lock or canAuthenticate check, unlike UpdateThemePreferenceAction, but Eloquent writes only the dirty locale column, so the worst outcome is a language code on a tombstone that never signs in or receives mail. Note for whoever fixes 02-56 anyway: docs/architecture/user-lifecycle.md:402-409 states that locale preferences already re-read under lock and require canAuthenticate, which the code does not do, so the doc currently overstates the barrier.
findings.resolution_ru: Запись локали без блокировки может попасть на аккаунт, анонимизированный в промежутке. Итог: та же находка, что 02-56, худший исход это код языка у tombstone; но user-lifecycle.md утверждает, что локаль перечитывается под блокировкой, а код этого не делает, это надо учесть при правке.

findings.claim: The own-post vote check should be re-run on the locked actor and post so a dirty caller-supplied Post cannot bypass ownership.
findings.reasoning: Same root cause as batch-02 02-70 (INVALID): canVote() is re-evaluated on the locked actor (VotePostAction.php:73-77) and posts.user_id is never reassigned, so the pre-lock ownership check (:52) cannot go stale. Both callers pass a Post read from the database (PostVoting.php:22-27 getPostProperty; ExecuteStudioAction.php:494-504 locked withTrashed read that also re-checks the author), so no 'dirty' Post reaches the action.
findings.resolution_ru: Проверку голоса за свой пост надо повторять на заблокированных акторе и посте. Итог: бот ошибся, как в 02-70: canVote() перепроверяется под блокировкой, posts.user_id не переназначается, а оба вызывающих передают Post из базы, грязный Post не попадает.

findings.claim: ensureAllowed() authorizes from an unlocked pre-transaction read, so a just-demoted or sanctioned admin can still retry, resume, cancel or stop.
findings.reasoning: Documented deadlock-avoidance decision, same as batch-01 INVALID 01-17: ManagesStudioActions.php:11-22 explains the administrator is read 'as it is now, without a lock' because the executor locks action rows before user rows. ensureAllowed (:26-33) still re-reads the current row and requires manage-studio-plans (role and lifecycle). Retry/Resume/Cancel/Stop only re-queue or cancel already-approved work, so a revocation racing them has no harmful consequence.
findings.resolution_ru: ensureAllowed() авторизует без блокировки, и разжалованный администратор ещё может повторить, возобновить, отменить или остановить. Итог: бот ошибся, это задокументированное решение против deadlock, как в 01-17; права перечитываются, а операции лишь трогают одобренную работу.

findings.claim: The executor switch authorizes the admin outside the transaction without a lock, so a sanction committing in between still lets the switch be flipped.
findings.reasoning: SwitchStudioExecutionAction.php:41-45 re-reads the current admin row (not the request-start instance) and requires both manage-studio-plans and manage-project-settings; the window is the milliseconds before the settings-row write (:47-54) in one in-flight request on a Filament page whose persistent Authenticate re-checks every request. It follows the same unlocked fresh-read pattern documented for the Action queue (ManagesStudioActions.php:11-22, 01-17) and the stale-actor SKIPs 01-35/02-14; the write only toggles execution of already-approved plans.
findings.resolution_ru: Переключатель исполнителя авторизует администратора вне транзакции без блокировки. Итог: верно в теории, но действие перечитывает текущую строку админа и требует двух прав, окно в миллисекунды, паттерн тот же, что в 01-17 и 01-35, а запись лишь переключает исполнение одобренных планов.

findings.claim: restart() resets attempts to 0, so a stale worker holding an old attempt number can pass the run/stop/postpone fence of a later retry with the same number.
findings.reasoning: The ABA needs a worker still alive with a claimed attempt after the action was failed, retried and re-claimed at the same number. restart() only applies to Failed/Held actions (Retry/Resume lockedIn, RetryStudioActionAction.php:42, ResumeStudioActionAction.php:39); the job carries only the action id and takes its attempt from the row at claim time (ExecuteStudioAction.php claim(), 'return $action->attempts'), so queued duplicates cannot bring an old number. A worker past its claim is killed at 75 s (ExecuteStudioActionJob.php:16-31, $timeout 75, failOnTimeout) while a Running action is only taken back after running_stale_after_seconds 180 'past the job's 75 s timeout' (docs/architecture/studio-plans.md configuration table), so no stale worker survives into a later attempt; and any run still re-checks every row under lock.
findings.resolution_ru: restart() сбрасывает attempts в 0, и устаревший воркер со старым номером может пройти проверку новой попытки. Итог: бот ошибся, job берёт номер попытки из строки при claim, воркер убивается через 75 с, а Running забирается только через 180 с, так что старый воркер не доживает.

findings.claim: settlePlan's open-action check is a plain read; under REPEATABLE READ it uses a snapshot taken before the plan lock wait, so two concurrent final actions can both see the other open and leave the plan Running forever.
findings.reasoning: On PostgreSQL (the primary and deployed engine, READ COMMITTED) each statement sees the latest commits, so the run that gets the plan lock second sees the first one Done and settles. On MariaDB (a supported compatibility target, CI mariadb:11.4, .github/workflows/ci.yml:660) InnoDB's REPEATABLE READ snapshot is fixed at the run's first non-locking read, which happens before any lock wait: doneParent()'s find() (ExecuteStudioAction.php:699) precedes lockActorAndPostAuthor and the plan lock. The later exists() in settlePlan (SettlesStudioPlan.php:29-32) then still sees the other action Running; nothing else settles a plan afterwards (the dispatcher never does), only an admin Stop. The executor race tests run against PostgreSQL only (docs/architecture/studio-plans.md 'Testing it').
findings.scenario: On a MariaDB installation, the last two votes of a plan (different Personas) run on two workers at once; each run's settlement sees the other still Running, both commit Done, and the plan shows Running indefinitely.

findings.claim: The executor and the dispatcher read the execution switch once, outside any coordination with SwitchStudioExecutionAction, so a switch-off committed just after the check still lets a claim or send happen.
findings.reasoning: ExecuteStudioAction::handle checks isOn() before claim() (:157-162) and DispatchDueStudioActionsAction checks it once per run (:60-62). A switch-off landing in that gap behaves exactly like one landing just after the claim, which the documented contract accepts ('a run a worker already claimed finishes', docs/architecture/studio-plans.md 'The switch'); actions the dispatcher sends after the flip are skipped by the executor's own check and later re-sent. Making a kill switch linearizable with every claim would need the settings-row lock on the hot path for a millisecond window.
findings.resolution_ru: Исполнитель и диспетчер читают переключатель один раз без координации с SwitchStudioExecutionAction. Итог: верно, но выключение в этом зазоре равно выключению сразу после claim, что контракт допускает; иначе нужна блокировка строки настроек на горячем пути ради миллисекунд.

findings.claim: An unexpected exception in a run is turned into a failed action without being reported, so operators never get the stack trace.
findings.reasoning: The catch (Throwable) branch (ExecuteStudioAction.php:184-201) calls report() only when the run had already committed (:186-192); otherwise it calls stop(UnexpectedFailure), which stores only the class in failure_reason (:819) and logs studio.action.failed without the exception (logReleased). handle() then returns normally, so the queue worker never reports it either (ExecuteStudioActionJob::handle has no catch). report() is the established Sentry path (bootstrap/app.php:38-46, used by DispatchDueStudioActionsAction.php:182 and here at :188); the class-only rule (docs/architecture/studio-plans.md:1382-1383) is about the stored failure_reason, not about Sentry.
findings.scenario: A code defect (TypeError, unexpected QueryException) makes every comment action of a plan fail with unexpected_failure; the admin sees 'Failed' and an exception class, but Sentry has nothing, so the cause cannot be diagnosed without reproducing it.

findings.claim: Rate-limit hits taken by the delegated vote/comment/post actions are not rolled back when the executor's outer transaction fails, consuming the Persona's window for writes that never happened.
findings.reasoning: True: VotePostAction (VotePostAction.php:56-65) and the other site actions hit the cache-backed limiter before their transaction, so a rolled-back run keeps one hit. The hit decays with the window (vote 60 s, comment 60 s, upload 600 s), an exhausted window only postpones the action rather than failing it (postpone(), ExecuteStudioAction.php:876), and members get the same non-transactional limiter. 'Permanently rate-limited' is not reachable; a transaction-aware quota is out of proportion.
findings.resolution_ru: Попадания в rate-limit от делегированных действий не откатываются при сбое транзакции исполнителя. Итог: верно, но попадание истекает с окном, исчерпанное окно лишь откладывает действие, у участников тот же лимитер; вечной блокировки нет, транзакционная квота несоразмерна.

findings.claim: Stop leaves a Running action to finish, but if that run is rate-limited, postpone() returns it to Pending and the dispatcher later runs it, so something is still published after the stop.
findings.reasoning: Stop cancels only Pending/Held/Failed/Dispatched actions (StopStudioPlanAction.php:64-69) and settlePlan keeps the plan Running while an action is Running (SettlesStudioPlan.php:29-36). A run that then meets the Persona's limit is postponed: postpone() turns the still-Running attempt back to Pending (ExecuteStudioAction.php:876-912). Nothing records the stop: the dispatcher's due check has no plan condition (DispatchDueStudioActionsAction.php:82-86) and publishComment only requires the plan to be Running (ExecuteStudioAction.php publishComment), which it still is. The docblock promises 'A run already claimed is left to finish ... so nothing follows it'; a postponed run did not finish. ManageStudioActionsTest covers Stop only without a concurrent run.
findings.scenario: An admin clicks Stop remaining actions on a historical plan while one Persona comment is mid-run and hits the commenting limit; the comment goes back to Pending and is published a minute later on a plan the admin stopped.

findings.claim: Stop reads the plan status without a lock and never re-checks it after locking the plan, so it can report success for a plan that just completed.
findings.reasoning: True (StopStudioPlanAction.php:54-62 unlocked read, plan locked at :87), but there is no transition back to Draft, and if a final action settled the plan in between, Stop finds no open actions, cancels nothing and settlePlan rewrites the same Completed/Cancelled status (SettlesStudioPlan.php:38-44: Completed iff the CreatePost is Done). The only effect is a 'stopped, 0 cancelled' log and toast instead of 'not running'.
findings.resolution_ru: Stop читает статус плана без блокировки и не перепроверяет его, поэтому может отчитаться об успехе для завершённого плана. Итог: верно, но возврата в Draft нет, Stop ничего не отменит, а settlePlan запишет тот же статус; эффект лишь лог и тост '0 отменено'.

findings.claim: The reload after the atomic claim may return a batch no longer Running, so the job sends a paid request for a batch another worker ended.
findings.reasoning: A text batch row never changes attempt_id (each request inserts a new row, RequestStudioPostTextGenerationAction.php:138-147), and a just-claimed batch cannot be ended as lost: the request only ends batches that are not underway, and a Running batch counts from started_at, set by the claim itself (StudioPlanTextGeneration::isStale, :95-104). A Request that locked the row first and failed it makes the claim's 'status = queued' UPDATE match nothing. The job also re-checks the plan before sending and CompleteStudioPostTextGenerationAction re-checks attempt and Running under lock.
findings.resolution_ru: После атомарного claim пакет может быть уже не Running, и job отправит платный запрос. Итог: бот ошибся, attempt_id пакета не меняется, только что взятый пакет нельзя завершить как потерянный, а job и CompleteStudioPostTextGenerationAction перепроверяют всё под блокировкой.

findings.claim: The reload after the claim is not constrained to the claimed attempt and Running status, so it can return a replacement attempt.
findings.reasoning: Unlike text batches, the analysis row is reused: RequestStudioImageAnalysisAction starts anew whenever the plan's photo changed, even while an attempt runs (startsAnew, :162-173; reset at :107-126). If that commits between the claim UPDATE (StartStudioImageAnalysisAction.php:23-31) and the reload (:43), the job gets attempt B's row, passes the stale-photo check against the new photo (AnalyzeStudioPlanImageJob isFor) and pays for an analysis that CompleteStudioImageAnalysisAction then discards by attempt. The window is one statement wide, so the cost is at most one wasted provider call; nothing wrong is stored.
findings.scenario: An admin replaces a plan's photo, and its new analysis request commits in the instant a worker claims the old attempt; the old job analyzes the new photo and its result is thrown away, a second paid call beside the new attempt's.

findings.claim: StudioPlan::save() results are ignored, so a vetoing saving listener would leave the action reporting success.
findings.reasoning: Same as batch-02 02-29/02-46 (SKIP): save() returns false only when a model listener vetoes, and StudioPlan has no booted()/observer/ObservedBy and no eloquent.* listener is registered anywhere in app/. Checking it would be consistency with the Studio code that already does (e.g. ApproveStudioPlanAction), not a fix.
findings.resolution_ru: Результат StudioPlan::save() игнорируется, и вето слушателя оставит действие с отчётом об успехе. Итог: так же, как 02-29 и 02-46, у StudioPlan нет ни booted(), ни observer, ни слушателей eloquent.*; проверка была бы согласованностью с остальным кодом Studio, а не исправлением.

findings.claim: The studio_plan.updated / image.removed logs run before an enclosing transaction commits.
findings.reasoning: Same as batch-02 02-61: no caller wraps these actions in a transaction. UpdateStudioPlanAction is called from CreateStudioPlan::save (CreateStudioPlan.php:112) and EditStudioPlan (EditStudioPlan.php:207), RemoveStudioPlanImageAction from EditsStudioPlan.php:403, all directly from Livewire methods; the log lines run after the actions' own transactions committed.
findings.resolution_ru: Логи studio_plan.updated и image.removed пишутся до коммита внешней транзакции. Итог: бот ошибся, как и в 02-61, никто не оборачивает эти действия в транзакцию, их вызывают прямо из методов Livewire, и логи идут после коммита собственных транзакций.

findings.claim: Concurrent draft deletions sharing an asset can each see the other's reference and both skip releasing it.
findings.reasoning: A Draft's photo is never shared: SetStudioPlanImageAction always inserts a fresh MediaAsset (MediaAssetCreator::create, MediaAssetCreator.php:30) and nothing else assigns studio_plans.image_asset_id (grep: only SetStudioPlanImage/Remove/Create). The only other referrer is the post the executor creates from an approved plan, and only Drafts can be deleted (currentDraft, LocksStudioPlanDraft.php:62-79). The physical purge re-checks references anyway (02-59).
findings.resolution_ru: Параллельное удаление черновиков с общим ассетом может помешать обоим освободить его. Итог: бот ошибся, фото черновика никогда не общее, SetStudioPlanImageAction всегда создаёт новый MediaAsset, удалять можно только Draft, а физическая очистка всё равно перепроверяет ссылки (02-59).

findings.claim: Batches ended as lost are marked Failed without finished_at.
findings.reasoning: RequestStudioPostTextGenerationAction.php:131-134 sets only status and error_code, while every other way a batch ends sets finished_at (FailStudioPostTextGenerationAction.php:37, CompleteStudioPostTextGenerationAction.php:73) and the discussion counterpart sets it on its lost rows (RequestStudioDiscussionGenerationAction.php:227-231). The column is documented as the batch's timings (docs/architecture/studio-plans.md 'What is kept'). Nothing reads it today, so the impact is data quality only.
findings.scenario: A batch whose worker died is ended as lost by the next request and keeps finished_at NULL forever, unlike every other ended batch.

findings.claim: The author's row should be locked too, or a concurrent Persona profile edit wastes the paid request or yields text without the author's voice.
findings.reasoning: The author's voice is part of the batch's source hash (StudioPostTextContext::sourceHash, stored at :142), and both the job before sending (GenerateStudioPostTextsJob.php:74-90) and CompleteStudioPostTextGenerationAction under lock (:58-64) refuse a batch whose hash no longer matches, so text in an old voice is never kept. Locking the author for the request transaction would not stop an edit committed right after it, which these re-checks already handle.
findings.resolution_ru: Нужно блокировать и строку автора, иначе правка профиля Persona сожжёт платный запрос. Итог: бот ошибся, голос автора входит в хеш источника пакета, и устаревший хеш отклоняют и job, и CompleteStudioPostTextGenerationAction; блокировка не остановила бы правку после транзакции.

findings.claim: discussionHash fingerprints category and tag ids while the prompt sends their names, so a rename does not mark a generation stale.
findings.reasoning: Accurate (StudioDiscussionContext.php:107-116), and it makes the class docblock's 'Everything the model is sent is in one of them' (:28-32) slightly untrue. But the effect is only that an AI-drafted discussion, which an admin reviews before approval, was written knowing a taxonomy label's previous name; and changing the hash formula would mark every stored generation of every draft stale. Not worth it beyond correcting the docblock.
findings.resolution_ru: discussionHash учитывает id категорий и тегов, а в промпт уходят их имена, и переименование не помечает генерацию устаревшей. Итог: верно, но эффект лишь в старом названии в черновике, который проверяет админ, а смена формулы хеша устарит все генерации; максимум поправить docblock.

findings.claim: Rating options can be archived or deleted between validatedAgainst() and write(), so a save accepts an option that is no longer active.
findings.reasoning: Documented intent: rating configuration stays its own to change and 'an option deleted or archived later leaves the vote naming it ... to be found by the checks before approval' (2026_10_21_100000_create_studio_plan_votes_table.php:61-64). Approval's preflight refuses such votes (vote_option_unavailable, docs/architecture/studio-plans.md:133), and the executor refuses inactive options again at run time (rating_option_unavailable). A save is a Draft; nothing is cast from it.
findings.resolution_ru: Опцию рейтинга могут архивировать между validatedAgainst() и write(), и сохранение примет неактивную опцию. Итог: бот ошибся, это задокументированный замысел: такие голоса отклоняют preflight одобрения и исполнитель, а сохранение это лишь Draft.

findings.claim: Keep as is writes generation state but emits no domain log event.
findings.reasoning: A request for extra observability: the action only records a text fingerprint on a Draft's generation so the editor stops warning (KeepStudioDiscussionAction.php:44-55); nothing is published or approved by it, and approval itself is logged. No defect.
findings.resolution_ru: Keep as is пишет состояние генерации, но не выдаёт доменное событие лога. Итог: это запрос на дополнительную наблюдаемость, действие лишь записывает отпечаток текста в генерации черновика, ничего не публикует и не одобряет, а само одобрение логируется; дефекта нет.

findings.claim: Single-line translation fields accept U+2028/U+2029 because only \n is checked.
findings.reasoning: True (UpdateProjectTranslationAction.php:105, 149), but the text comes only from administrators with manage-project-settings or from the AI provider, cannot be typed into an input by accident, and json_encode escapes these characters for scripts by default. Consistent with batch-02 02-44/02-27 (admin-input hardening, SKIP); impact would be cosmetic.
findings.resolution_ru: Однострочные поля перевода принимают U+2028/U+2029. Итог: верно, но текст приходит только от администраторов с manage-project-settings или от AI-провайдера, случайно его не ввести, а json_encode экранирует эти символы; это укрепление ввода админа с косметическим эффектом.

findings.claim: forgetActive() is a non-atomic get-then-delete outside the language lock, so it can delete the pointer of a batch started in between.
findings.reasoning: Mechanically true (ProjectTranslationGenerationStore.php:154-159 GET then DEL; StartProjectTranslationGenerationAction.php:88-107 writes the pointer under lockLanguage). But the active pointer is per administrator and language, so the race is the same administrator pressing 'Discard all' in one tab and 'Generate missing' in another within the microseconds between a Redis GET and DEL; Start's current() would even return the old batch if it still had ready suggestions. Same class as batch-02 02-39/02-53 (one user racing themselves, SKIP).
findings.resolution_ru: forgetActive() делает GET и DEL не атомарно и вне блокировки языка и может удалить указатель нового пакета. Итог: верно механически, но указатель свой у каждого админа и языка, гонка это один админ в двух вкладках за микросекунды; тот же класс, что 02-39 и 02-53.

findings.claim: Two concurrent discards of the same suggestion both succeed, though an already-discarded one should be refused.
findings.reasoning: True (both pass the ready check at :46, the second resolve changes nothing, and :65 sees Discarded), but the end state is identical either way: the suggestion is discarded once and nothing else changes. Only the second tab's response says 'discarded' instead of 'not ready'.
findings.resolution_ru: Два параллельных discard одной подсказки оба успешны, хотя второй должен быть отклонён. Итог: верно, но конечное состояние одинаково: подсказка отброшена один раз, больше ничего не меняется; лишь вторая вкладка видит 'discarded' вместо 'not ready'.

findings.claim: Discarding the last ready suggestion one by one leaves an empty completed batch as active, so reloads show stale generation state.
findings.reasoning: The state shown is accurate, not stale: the reload returns the batch summary ('0 AI suggestions ready - N saved - M discarded', script.blade.php:554-573) and keeps failed/skipped row messages, and Generate missing is offered because offersGenerate is '!running && readyCount === 0' (script.blade.php:551-553). Start treats a completed batch with no ready items as none and creates a new one (StartProjectTranslationGenerationAction.php:128-141). Saving the last suggestions individually leaves the batch the same way; only bulk discard is documented to let it go (:23-24).
findings.resolution_ru: Поштучный discard последней подсказки оставляет пустой завершённый пакет активным. Итог: бот ошибся, показанное состояние точное: видна сводка пакета и доступен Generate missing, а Start считает такой пакет пустым и создаёт новый.

findings.claim: The English source or the stored target can change while the provider request is in flight, and the interactive suggestion is later saved through the unguarded handle().
findings.reasoning: True that the checks (:83-93) precede translate() (:96-97). But an interactive suggestion is documented as an ordinary draft that becomes content only when an administrator saves it through UpdateProjectTranslationAction 'like any other draft' (:21-26), and manual saves are deliberately unguarded (docs/architecture/translation-engine.md 'Save stays explicit': 'The ordinary handle() has no guard and still replaces a stored translation, as a manual save must'). Re-checking after translate() would not help, since the save comes later from the same page; guarding it means stale-tab protection for every manual draft, a feature rather than a fix.
findings.resolution_ru: Исходник или перевод могут измениться во время запроса к провайдеру, а подсказка потом сохраняется через handle() без защиты. Итог: верно, но подсказка это обычный черновик, а ручное сохранение намеренно без защиты; защита всех черновиков от устаревших вкладок это фича.

findings.claim: A Save that read the item as Ready can still publish it after a concurrent Discard of the same item.
findings.reasoning: Mechanically true: the Ready read (:64-68) and the write (:96) are not under the batch lock, and Discard resolves under that lock only. But the batch is owned by one administrator (ownedBatch), so the race is that administrator clicking Save and Discard on the same suggestion at the same moment (two tabs, or both requests in flight from TranslationCenterPage.php:196/234); the result is the suggestion they also asked to save being saved. The guarded write still refuses outdated or already-translated units (:96-102). Same class as 02-39/02-53.
findings.resolution_ru: Save, прочитавший элемент как Ready, может опубликовать его после параллельного Discard. Итог: верно механически, но пакет принадлежит одному админу, гонка это его одновременные Save и Discard с итогом, о котором он тоже просил; тот же класс, что 02-39 и 02-53.

findings.claim: If the request dies between storing the batch and dispatching its jobs, the queued chunks are never sent and the batch is not recovered.
findings.reasoning: Handled by documented design: a dispatch that throws fails that chunk and every later one (:151-163), and a chunk no worker took within translation.bulk.stale_queued_seconds (3600) is failed on the next read, 'a queue that lost the job, or has no worker', so the language is not held for the batch's lifetime (docs/architecture/translation-engine.md 'Locks only around state'; ProjectTranslationGenerationStore.php:41-48). Republishing chunks automatically would risk a second paid call, which the design forbids ('generating again is the administrator's choice').
findings.resolution_ru: Если запрос умрёт между сохранением пакета и отправкой jobs, чанки не уйдут. Итог: бот ошибся, это покрыто дизайном: упавший dispatch проваливает чанки, а не взятый за 3600 с чанк проваливается при чтении; автоповтор рисковал бы вторым платным вызовом.

findings.claim: The backfill overwrites malformed (non-string) per-locale translation values instead of counting them as skipped_unknown.
findings.reasoning: True in fill() (:291-302) and staticPages() (:215-228): a non-string locale value is not isPresent() and would be replaced. But the branch is unreachable today: the repository ships English only (config/static-pages.php defaults have only 'en'; the class docblock :26-28 says a deploy 'lends no translation'), so $entry->value($locale) is null and the entry is skipped_unknown. No application path writes a non-string translation value either; and such a value is never shown to anyone (TranslatableField::resolve falls back to English).
findings.resolution_ru: Backfill перезаписывает нестроковые значения переводов вместо учёта как skipped_unknown. Итог: верно, но ветка сейчас недостижима: поставляется только английский, нестроковые значения никто не пишет, а показать их нельзя, TranslatableField::resolve берёт английский.

findings.claim: The PR description lacks the template's verification, architecture, visual and mobile sections.
findings.reasoning: Audit-PR bookkeeping, not a property of the code (same as 01-37/02-88).
findings.resolution_ru: В описании PR нет разделов шаблона про верификацию, архитектуру, визуал и мобильную проверку. Итог: это служебное оформление аудитного PR, а не свойство кода, как и 01-37 и 02-88.

findings.claim: CommentsSection's public $postId is client-writable and CommentListQuery never checks the parent post, so the comment thread of a hidden, author-deleted or otherwise non-public post can be read.
findings.reasoning: CommentsSection.php:20 is an unlocked public int (the project locks such ids elsewhere, e.g. FollowButton.php:18 #[Locked]); comments()/totalComments()/totalRenderableTopLevel() hand it straight to CommentListQuery (CommentsSection.php:32-52), whose visibleForPost()/renderableTopLevelForPost() filter only post_id and comment status (CommentListQuery.php:68-104) — no post status or deleted_at condition. Normal UI only mounts the section for published posts (post-drawer via PublishedPostDetailsQuery, post-show), so the gap needs a forged Livewire update, but post ids are sequential and the section works for guests. docs/architecture/post-lifecycle.md:95-98 says a deleted post is 'publicly gone everywhere', and comment-lifecycle.md:85-86 treats Hidden/author-deleted parents as non-public surfaces.
findings.scenario: A guest opens any published post and sends a Livewire update setting the comments-section's postId to the id of a post a moderator hid (or one its author deleted, still in retention); the response renders that post's whole visible thread with author names.

findings.claim: submit() downloads the client-settable importedImageUrl without checking allow_url_imports, and before the create ability, the upload rate limit and field validation run.
findings.reasoning: Same root cause as 02-41 (BUG low), seen from the component: UploadPostForm.php:90-101 calls StoreImportedImageAction::download() for the public $importedImageUrl (:49) before $this->validate() (:104) and before CreatePostAction's can('create') and upload rate limit (CreatePostAction.php:59-68); neither submit() nor download() checks allow_url_imports — only the view hides the URL tab (upload-post-form.blade.php:149-163). Livewire accepts 50 calls per request (config/livewire.php:279), so one request can trigger up to 50 fetches of up to the 5 MB ingest cap. The rabbit 90-104 item (authorize/rate-limit/validate first) is the same unguarded ordering and is fixed in the same place.
findings.scenario: A signed-in member — even a Limited one who may not post — loops Livewire submit calls with importedImageUrl pointing at any public host and an empty title; the server downloads the image every time, unthrottled and even with URL imports switched off, then validation fails and the temp file is deleted.

findings.claim: After a successful save the $avatar upload is never cleared, so every later save on the same page re-ingests it as a new avatar.
findings.reasoning: save() passes $this->avatar to UpdateUserProfileAction::execute() (EditProfileForm.php:58) and never resets it, so the TemporaryUploadedFile stays in component state. execute() stores a new file and creates a new MediaAsset whenever $avatar !== null (UpdateUserProfileAction.php:38-41, 64-68), soft-deletes the previous asset while deliberately leaving its file on disk (:73-81), and dispatches variant generation (:104). No test saves twice (tests/Feature/Livewire/AvatarUploadTest.php).
findings.scenario: A member picks a new avatar and presses Save, then edits the bio and presses Save again: a second identical avatar asset and full-size file are created, the first asset is soft-deleted with its files left on disk, and variants are generated again — once per further save. If Livewire has pruned the temp upload in between, the later save fails instead.

findings.claim: The /saved page and the profile's Saved tab ignore the show_saved_posts flag, so saved posts stay reachable after the feature is switched off.
findings.reasoning: docs/saved-posts/saved-posts.md:17-23 states that all saved-posts UI is gated by show_saved_posts. SavedPostsPage::render (SavedPostsPage.php:17-34) and the /saved route (routes/web.php:83) never check it; ProfilePage adds the 'saved' tab for the owner unconditionally (ProfilePage.php:52-61, 86-94), the tab button renders for any owner (profile-page.blade.php:125-133) and ProfileStats counts saved posts for the owner (ProfileStats.php:23-25, shown at profile-page.blade.php:94-97). Only the save buttons, nav links and the save/unsave actions check the flag.
findings.scenario: An administrator turns show_saved_posts off; members still see a 'Saved' count and tab on their own profile and can open it, or /saved, to browse their saved list as if the feature were on.

findings.claim: Deleting a post from the drawer never emits post-deleted, so the list behind it keeps showing the deleted card.
findings.reasoning: deleteSelectedPost() (PostDrawer.php:75-103) only clears its own postId and dispatches clear-selected-post; the only post-deleted dispatcher is FeedPage::deletePost (FeedPage.php:152), used by the card's delete. PostFeed re-renders only on post-deleted/post-uploaded/post-moderated/comment events (PostFeed.php:32-43) and, as a keyed child without reactive props, is not re-rendered by FeedPage handling clear-selected-post. No test calls deleteSelectedPost.
findings.scenario: The author opens their post in the drawer (split view or the overlay) and deletes it from the drawer menu: the drawer closes, but the post's card stays in the feed until a full reload; clicking it opens an 'unavailable' panel.

findings.claim: The bell lists only the 10 latest notifications while the badge counts every unread one, so older unread notifications can never be reached or marked read.
findings.reasoning: unreadCount counts all unread (NotificationBell.php:13-22) but the dropdown shows the latest 10 regardless of read state (:27-38), and 'Mark as read' exists only on listed rows (notification-bell.blade.php, mark-notification-read). There is no mark-all action, no notifications page, and opening a notification link does not mark it read (no other read_at write in app/ or routes/).
findings.scenario: A member receives 14 notifications while away and marks the 10 shown as read; the 4 older unread ones never appear in the list, so the badge shows 4 permanently with no way to clear it.

findings.claim: visibleCount is client-writable and CommentListQuery applies it as an uncapped limit, so one request can load a post's entire comment tree.
findings.reasoning: $visibleCount is an unlocked public int (CommentsSection.php:24) passed as the limit to CommentListQuery::get(), which only applies max(1, $limit) (CommentListQuery.php:42) and eager-loads every visible reply of each root (:18-31). The server only changes it in loadMore() (+5) and setCommentSort() (reset to 5) (:54-71). A user could reach the same state with many clicks, so this is an amplification of one request rather than new access.
findings.scenario: A script sets visibleCount to 1,000,000 on a busy post: one request loads every root comment and reply and renders a CommentVoting child (two queries each) for all of them.

findings.claim: deleteComment/hideComment let CannotDeleteCommentException/CannotHideCommentException escape as a 500, and canDeleteComment() does not match all of the action's refusals.
findings.reasoning: Both methods call the actions without a catch (CommentsSection.php:169-201); the exceptions are plain DomainExceptions with no render mapping. canDeleteComment() mirrors only CommentPolicy::delete (:204-209), while DeleteCommentAction also refuses finalized removals and comments under a post that can no longer receive comments (DeleteCommentAction.php:51-71). In practice the mismatch is reached only through races: the section renders only for published posts and finalized comments render as button-less tombstones; HideCommentAction treats already-hidden/deleted targets as no-ops, so hide fails only for a moderator sanctioned mid-page. The Filament list catches the same refusals (ListComments.php:359).
findings.scenario: A member has a published post's thread open; a moderator hides the post; the member clicks Delete on their own comment and gets Livewire's server-error modal instead of a message.

findings.claim: Voting one comment re-renders every CommentVoting component in the thread, because each listens to the global comment-voted event without filtering.
findings.reasoning: vote() dispatches comment-voted (CommentVoting.php:54) and every instance listens with an empty handler (:57-61), which re-renders it; each render runs two queries (comment and current vote, :63-70; CommentVotingService.php:17-35). The voting component re-renders itself after its own action anyway, so the listener only adds work.
findings.scenario: Upvoting one comment in a drawer that shows 40 comments makes the follow-up request re-render 40 CommentVoting components, about 80 queries.

findings.claim: SavePostButton::mount() runs Post::find() and a saved-state query for every card although a batched loader exists.
findings.reasoning: mount() runs Post::find($postId) and SavedPostState::forUserAndPost() per instance (SavePostButton.php:30-36), and a button is mounted on every card for signed-in users (post-card.blade.php:131). SavedPostState::forUserAndPosts() batches this (tested in tests/Feature/Support/SavedPostStateN1Test.php) and docs/saved-posts/saved-posts.md says to use it on feed pages, but nothing calls it.
findings.scenario: A signed-in member's 12-card feed (or saved page) spends 24 extra queries on save buttons per render.

findings.claim: Every RatingVoting child re-reads its rating group and options on each render, an N×G query pattern on the feed.
findings.reasoning: render() and vote() call RatingConfigurationManager::activeGroupByKey() (RatingVoting.php:83, 108), which runs a group query plus an options eager load each time with no per-request memo (RatingConfigurationManager.php:25-32). PostFeed already loads activeGroups() once and preloads distribution and selection (PostFeed.php:61-68), so only this configuration read remains per card and group.
findings.scenario: A 12-card feed with two rating groups runs about 48 configuration queries per render, repeated on every feed re-render.

findings.claim: PostVoting, mounted per feed card with only a postId, re-queries the published post and the viewer's vote for every card.
findings.reasoning: The post accessor re-reads the post through published()->find() (PostVoting.php:23-28) and currentVoteFor() queries post_votes (:114-124) on each render; the component sits on every card (post-card.blade.php:20) and in the drawer, while PostFeed already holds the posts and could batch the viewer's votes as it does rating state.
findings.scenario: A signed-in 12-card feed render spends 24 queries on vote rails.

findings.claim: Each nested CommentVoting component queries its comment and the viewer's vote on render, an N+1 over the comment thread.
findings.reasoning: render() calls CommentVotingService::comment() and currentVote() per instance (CommentVoting.php:63-70; CommentVotingService.php:17-35), although CommentListQuery has already loaded every rendered comment with its counters. Thread size is bounded by visibleCount roots plus their replies (see 04-07), and 04-09 multiplies this cost on every vote.
findings.scenario: A drawer showing 30 comments to a member runs about 60 extra queries per render.

findings.claim: toggle() inverts whatever the database holds rather than applying the state the button shows, and instances for the same post never sync, so a stale button undoes the user's intent.
findings.reasoning: SavePostButton::toggle() calls ToggleSavedPostAction, which flips post_saves (ToggleSavedPostAction.php:17-32), and no event updates other instances. On the feed in split view the card's button (post-card.blade.php:131) and the drawer's (post-drawer-content.blade.php:120) show the same post at the same time; SavedPostsPage does not refresh either. FollowButton, by contrast, syncs its instances (FollowButton.php:60, 68-75). Distinct from the concurrency race in 02-53.
findings.scenario: In split view the member saves a post from the drawer; the card still shows 'Save'; clicking it unsaves the post and the card again shows 'Save' — two Save clicks end with the post unsaved, while the drawer shows 'Saved'.

findings.claim: PostFeed::$selectedPostId is not reactive, so selecting a post never marks its card as selected.
findings.reasoning: FeedPage passes :selected-post-id to PostFeed (feed-page.blade.php:112-121), but the child's key no longer includes it (removed in commit 4fc401b7 so the feed is not remounted per click) and the property has no #[Reactive] (PostFeed.php:30). After FeedPage::selectPost() the child is not re-rendered, so post-card's 'selected-post' variant (post-card.blade.php:4, card.blade.php:11) is never applied, although feed-page.blade.php:66 says overlay mode 'always marks the selected card'.
findings.scenario: A member clicks a card and the drawer opens, but the card is never highlighted; after a filter change while a post is open, the highlight sticks to that post even after another is selected.

findings.claim: In overlay mode a selection dispatches post-selected twice, and the second can overwrite the overlay's return-focus target with the panel itself.
findings.reasoning: The feed's x-on:select-post calls FeedPage::selectPost() in overlay mode (feed-page.blade.php:68), which dispatches post-selected (FeedPage.php:122); the layout's overlay drawer also listens to select-post (PostDrawer.php:47-50) and dispatches post-selected again in setSelectedPost() (:65). The overlay's post-selected handler stores document.activeElement as returnFocusEl and then focuses itself (post-drawer.blade.php:49-53). If the two responses are processed in separate ticks, the second event records the panel as the return target; on the profile and saved pages only the drawer dispatches, so its dispatch is still needed there.
findings.scenario: A keyboard user opens a post from the feed in overlay mode and presses Escape: focus returns to the now-inert panel instead of the card, dropping them at the top of the page.

findings.claim: A failed delete from a feed card sets $deleteError, which nothing renders, so the failure is silent.
findings.reasoning: FeedPage::deletePost() stores the refusal in $deleteError (FeedPage.php:136-142), but only post-show and post-drawer-content render a deleteError; the card's confirm button closes its modal at once (post-card.blade.php:197-201). The button shows only when deleteFromFeed allows it, so a refusal needs a race (post hidden or author sanctioned meanwhile).
findings.scenario: An author confirms Delete on a card just after a moderator hid the post: the modal closes, nothing changes and no message explains why.

findings.claim: A failed deletion message persists when the overlay drawer shows another post.
findings.reasoning: deleteError (PostDrawer.php:95) is cleared only when deleteSelectedPost() runs again (:77, :101); setSelectedPost() (:55-66) and closeOverlay() (:69-73) keep it, and the drawer's delete dialog renders it (post-drawer-content.blade.php:206-207). Only the persistent layout overlay keeps state across posts.
findings.scenario: A delete in the overlay fails; the member opens another of their posts and its delete dialog already shows the previous post's error.

findings.claim: toggle() shows 'This author cannot be followed.' for both CannotFollowAuthorException reasons, blaming the author when the viewer's own account may not follow.
findings.reasoning: FollowAuthorAction throws followerNotAllowed() when the viewer is not Active (FollowAuthorAction.php:40-41, 60-61; UserStatus::canFollow is Active-only, UserStatus.php:58-61) and authorNotViewable() for the author, but FollowButton maps every CannotFollowAuthorException to follows.cannot_follow_author (FollowButton.php:63-64). The button renders for any non-self viewer (follow-button.blade.php:2), sanctioned ones included.
findings.scenario: A Limited member clicks Follow on a normal author and is told the author cannot be followed.

findings.claim: The user branch of resolveReportable() lets a member report their own account through a crafted request.
findings.reasoning: Same root cause as 02-73 (MINOR low): ReportModal's reportableType/reportableId are plain public properties and the 'user' branch resolves any user (ReportModal.php:75-76), the profile only hides the button for oneself (ProfilePage.php:114-118), and ReportContentAction has no self check for User targets.
findings.scenario: A member forges the report modal payload with their own user id; a report against their own account lands in the moderation queue.

findings.claim: The avatar rule accepts formats the ingest pipeline rejects, so users get a generic error instead of a field error.
findings.reasoning: avatarRules() is File::image()->max() (EditProfileForm.php:66-74); Laravel's image rule accepts jpeg/png/bmp/gif/webp (SVG only with allowSvg, so the SVG part of the claim is wrong), while uploads.images.mimes is jpg/jpeg/png/webp (config/uploads.php:17) and GdImageIngestor rejects other MIME types (GdImageIngestor.php:83-84). The rejection becomes the generic submitError plus a report() to Sentry (EditProfileForm.php:59-61).
findings.scenario: A member uploads a GIF avatar: validation passes, saving shows 'This image could not be processed', and an exception is reported for an ordinary user mistake.

findings.claim: effectiveSearch() uses strlen, so the 3-character minimum is measured in bytes and not enforced for Cyrillic input.
findings.reasoning: FeedPage.php:264 counts bytes; the app ships ru and bg locales, so two Cyrillic letters (4 bytes) pass while two Latin letters do not. The result drives both MatchedUsersQuery and PostFeed's LIKE search and the feed key (feed-page.blade.php:112-121).
findings.scenario: A Russian-speaking member typing 'ка' already triggers user search and a feed reload, while 'ab' does not.

findings.claim: The switcher marks 'system' when the user has no stored preference, ignoring the project default theme the layout actually applies.
findings.reasoning: mount() uses theme_preference or 'system' (ThemeSwitcher.php:17-21), while the layout applies ThemeManager::preferenceForUser(), which falls back to the project default_theme and normalizes invalid values (ThemeManager.php:13-38; AppServiceProvider.php View::composer), and theme-bootstrap.js uses that when localStorage is empty.
findings.scenario: An administrator sets the default theme to dark; a new visitor on a light-mode OS sees the dark site with the 'System' button pressed, and clicking System switches the site to light.

findings.claim: Every guest vote call writes a security-log line with no per-IP limit, so one visitor can grow the 30-day security log without bound.
findings.reasoning: RatingVoting::vote (RatingVoting.php:62-67), PostVoting::vote (:42-43) and CommentVoting::vote (:30-32) call GuestVoteAttemptLog::record() for each guest call; each line carries IP, a 512-char user agent and a 512-char referer (GuestVoteAttemptLog.php:27, 37-49) into the daily security channel kept 30 days (config/logging.php:81-87). Nothing throttles guests, and Livewire accepts 50 calls per request (config/livewire.php:279).
findings.scenario: A script sends Livewire requests each carrying 50 guest vote() calls; every request appends ~50 KB to the security log, burying real entries and filling disk.

findings.claim: An out-of-range page on /saved shows the 'no saved posts' empty state with no pagination links.
findings.reasoning: SavedPostsPage paginates by ?page (SavedPostsPage.php:22; SavedPostsQuery::forUser) and the view shows the empty state whenever the current page is empty, rendering links only otherwise (saved-posts-page.blade.php:4, 23). Unsaving, or a saved post being hidden or deleted, can empty the last page.
findings.scenario: A member on page 2 of their saved posts unsaves its only post and reloads: the page says they have no saved posts and offers no way back to page 1.

findings.claim: A successful submission clears body but leaves an earlier body error displayed.
findings.reasoning: addError('body', ...) (CommentForm.php:22, 34-39) persists across requests because Livewire stores property errors in the snapshot memo (SupportValidation::dehydrate), and reset('body') (:44) does not touch the error bag; nothing else resets it on success. The view keeps the error text and danger styling while $errors->has('body') (comment-form.blade.php:20-28).
findings.scenario: A member is refused for commenting too fast, waits, and submits again successfully: the comment appears and the textarea empties, but the rate-limit error stays under it.

findings.claim: The rating-activity list orders only by created_at, so tied votes at the 30-row cut can change between requests.
findings.reasoning: forProfile() uses ->latest()->limit($limit) (UserRatingActivityQuery.php:27-28) with no unique tie-breaker; votes on several groups of a post within one second, or Studio-dated votes, share a timestamp. docs/architecture/http-and-database-boundaries.md:118-121 requires a unique final order for listing queries and UserPublicPostsQuery follows it.
findings.scenario: A profile with more than 30 votes whose 30th and 31st share a timestamp shows a different last vote, or a different order, on each reload.

findings.claim: The Suspicious filter ignores author-deleted posts and comments, so deleting reported content takes a member off the list.
findings.reasoning: The filter uses whereHas('posts'/'comments', reports_count > 0) (ModerationUsersQuery.php:112-117), and those relations carry the SoftDeletes scope, while the reports column on the same list counts deleted content on purpose (reportsOnContent, :84-101, 'their authors' deleted ones included'); SuspiciousUsersWidget.php:30-40 uses the same predicate. The design contract defines suspicious as 'shadowbanned, or with reported posts or comments' (docs/design/admin/design-contract.md:1380-1381).
findings.scenario: A member whose post collected reports deletes it: the user list still shows reports against them, but they drop out of the Suspicious filter and the dashboard's Suspicious users count.

findings.claim: statusDecision() returns the latest sanction log even when the person's current status did not come from it, e.g. a Deleted account.
findings.reasoning: statusDecision() returns the newest Ban/Limit/Shadowban/Restore/Unban log for the person (UserModerationProfileQuery.php:54-64) regardless of the current status; self-deletion writes no such log, yet UserEditor shows the result as 'Since <date> by <moderator>' plus the sanction reason (UserEditor.php:170, 184-187). Deleted accounts are listed and openable (ModerationUsersQuery.php:145).
findings.scenario: A Limited member deletes their account; an admin opening the tombstone sees 'Deleted · Since 3 Mar by <moderator>' and the limit reason, as if that decision had produced the deletion.
findings.reconsidered_because: the mismatched decision can never be shown.
findings.resolution_ru: statusDecision() берёт последнюю санкцию, даже если текущий статус аккаунта, например Deleted, пришёл не из неё. Итог: оставили как есть, такое рассогласованное решение на экран не попадает.

findings.claim: categoryId defaults to '', which nullable does not skip, so integer rejects a submission without a category.
